Tour de Chicken Creek + Octoginta = October CycleFest

Last year we combined our two fall classic rides, the Octoginta and Tour de Chicken Creek into one weekend, and brought back an old favorite the Bicycle Swap Meet and added the EXPO, and named it the October CycleFest! Go to the LBC Website for details of all the events. This full weekend of cycling fun went over very well so we're doing it again. One change, however is that the Swap Meet will be much reduced in size and both it and the EXPO will be moved to Broken Arrow park on Sunday, coinciding with the Octoginta.

The CycleFest success depends on Volunteers like YOU, and the vast majority of the volunteers are members of the Lawrence Bicycle Club. This is an opportunity to give something back to the club.  Most volunteer positions are on the event's days, but some are in the days leading up to the weekend. Many people volunteer for one of the rides and then ride in the other.  Scroll through the volunteer slots and find one that fits for you.

Come play bikes with us! 

But…What is cyclocross anyway?!

Weellll…it's kinda like if a road bike and a mountain bike and a cross country running event all got mashed together!

Cyclocross is the best spectator friendly cycling event there is. ‘Cross races are held on short 1.5 to 2 mile laps that will mostly consist of grass and sometimes mud but can include sand, artificial barriers, hills, off camber sections, forced runs, and just about any dumb thing we can find in the park to make the race more fun to do but also to watch! We strive to make the race fun for everyone that comes out; from beginners and youth racers to the most experienced elite racers in Arkansas but especially to spectators! SHAM endeavors to make as much of the race course visible from as many spots along the way as possible, but especially at the start/finish line so you can cheer on  your friends and family and all the other racers out for a fun day in the sun…or mud…or maybe snow…but almost definitely sand and grass!

Welcome to the Arkansas Graveler

The Arkansas Graveler route winds through some of the most scenic, iconic rural roads of Arkansas. Daily ride distances average around 70 miles, with the option for a “fast & flat” century that highlights the Delta Heritage Trail State Park on the final day. 

This is a gravel TOUR, not a race. You’ll want to make the most of every farm stand, rest stop, and all the many grassroots flavors Arkansas has to offer.

For further details on what each category includes and the structure of our daily rides, please visit our website arkansasgraveler.com

Refunds/Transfers/Deferrals: 

We understand things come up and plans change! We do our best to give you a flexible refund/deferral program. However, the Arkansas Graveler is a complex, large-scale multi-day event. We enter into numerous pre-event contracts with cities, venues, caterers, entertainment producers, and ride support teams. Please see our refund policy below: 

  • Participants may receive a full refund minus a 15% admin fee until August 31, 2026, should they back out of the event.

  • Riders may also transfer their entry to another rider for no additional fee until October 4, 2026.

Cyclocross Race Training at Hale Education. 

Driving Directions: Hale’s South Entrance – next to 573 Dover Road, Westwood, MA, 02090 

We have fields, stairs, gravel, a sandpit, and a beach to ride, with fewerot rocks and roots than many of Hale's other trails.  

You can expect two twenty-minute heats and a multiple-lap course. 

Support MTB at Hale 

Mountain bikers of all ages are drawn to Hale’s rugged, varied terrain just miles from Boston’s city line, and we’ve been eagerly expanding youth mountain biking program over the past five years. 

Hale MTB Camp focuses on skill-building and ride time for an existing community of young mountain bikers. Youth MTB Club is growing that community through a fantastic team of volunteer coaches who coordinate recreational rides and opportunities to participate in races and events throughout New England. Intrepid Academy at Hale students also enjoy time on the trails as part of their semester at Hale. 

We’re thrilled with our progress and are helping hundreds of riders advance, but with your help, we can do more. 

Thank you for supporting MTB opportunities for youth by making your donation today. 

About Hale 

Hale is a nonprofit organization that serves nearly 16,000 people annually. We count on donations from people like you to help us provide an outdoor experience to the children in Greater Boston. Your gift today will help us continue to run great programs like this one, steward the land for our community, and ensure Greater Boston’s kids have transformational camp experiences. 

By registering for Hale’s events and programs, you consent to its privacy policy, media policy, and refund policies.

World famous Wednesday Worlds cyclocross practice at Holster Park, in Clifton NJ.

The best and only cyclocross training group in North Jersey – for over 10 years. 

Wednesday Worlds is FREE and run by local cyclocross racers. The goal is to grow the sport of cyclocross and give racers the opportunity to practice racing skills together.  We've been doing this for years and its always a good time. 

Wheels down 5:30 -Come early to get warmed up, the course is setup by 515pm.  Sessions are a mix of skills and drills to build fitness before moving on to FAST hard race efforts. Session ends around sunset depending on weather, daylight and conditions.  Meet at the benches in front of the tennis courts.  

Location:  https://www.google.com/maps/place/Holster+Park/@40.8593319,-74.188589,16z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x89c2ffb3b0eb8ab1:0xa15abc2860c1a7ec!8m2!3d40.8593319!4d-74.1860141!16s%2Fg%2F1tdwr0j4?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI0MDgyOC4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D

Important info:

  • This is a training group, not a race. Beginners are encouraged and very welcome, but be please be aware that cyclocross is physically demanding and requires a good level of fitness.   
  • We ride in a public park and conditions may change each week. We are guests in the park and will do everything to keep it clean and respect the rules.
  • We respect others in the park. We respect each other. No fighting. All are welcome.  
  • Helmet is required. Bring a cyclocross (or MTB) bike in good working order.
  • Park on the road between the school and the baseball field. Do NOT park in the fenced area behind the school.  
  • Event may be cancelled due to weather.  We ride if it rains but we cancel if stormy or if the park grounds are soaked.  Check your email and join the Facebook Group for the latest info.
  • Be nice to each other.
  • Questions? wednesdaycyclocross@gmail.com

-10/8  10:30am From  The Fountain: Trying to figure out a shuttle for this now that the train is not running. We will get some kind of ride in for sure. Pay attention to the StarCrawf Promotions Facebookk PageTrain Ride / Group Bike Ride.  Expect about 4 hours of pedaling with a little bit of everything, that shows off other trails that are not part of the WaterShed Trail System. 10:30am Thursday Ride, it looks like we will pedal from town / The Fountain on Front Street. We will explore Huckleberry State Forest  trails. 4 hours or so, there are bail outs if needed. -10/9 10:30am: Group ride trails and city, Departs from The Fountain. 3-4 hours with plenty of bail outs if needed.   We will ride some WST, town, special areas and some surprises. 4ish hours probably

Decider Competition and other games for Championship Round. 9:30ish Course reveal at Fox n Hare Brewery.

We will have a neutral police escort roll out from the fountain on Front St. at 10am SHARP!  So be there at 9:30!  then we will STOP! And regroup once we get to the trailhead. Expect about a 18-25mile loop, with bailouts and comfort stations. Maybe, Probably?? there will be a prize for the fastest Male and Female, but the champions / Tattoos will go to “Special “ riders, which also could be the fastest riders? Aka anyone could win.

Stoked!!!

Welcome to Cross Camp - four nights of cyclocross racing at the iconic Driveway in Austin, TX.

The rules are simple:

  1. Don’t be a jerk.
  2. Abide by all USAC cyclocross rules.
  3. The promoter’s ruling is final.
  4. Gravel and mountain bikes without bar ends are allowed. No maximum tire widths enforced.
  5. Please inform the finish line judges if you withdraw from the race.
  6. Prizes will be awarded 3 deep in competitive categories.
  7. Please patronize our sponsors.
  8. You must check in with the registration staff to be counted in the results.
  9. Absolutely no alochol is permitted on the grounds of The Driveway at any time. 


Entry Fees

Entry fees are $45 for your first race and includes any additional races on the same day (ex. Novice riders may also enter the 3/4 /Novice field on the same day at no additional cost).  Note: You must register for these at the same time to take advantage of this discount.

Season passes are available and will automatically enroll you for 4 nights of the category of your choosing. You may also select additional races throughout the series during your registration if you would like to race multiple categories on some (or all) nights.

Late registration is available this year. Entries after 12 pm the day of each race will incur a $5 late fee and may not be included in call ups. Registration closes 30 minutes before each race wave, so we highly encourage you to sign up as soon as you can!

Racing Licenses

All categories require a USA Cycling license to participate. If you do not have a current USAC annual license you can purchase one at memberships.usacycling.org. 

Course

You will race on +/- 1.5 mile courses taking in new trails connected by fast pavement for a course that's always changing.

 

Parking and directions

Ample parking is available at the Driveway, but we highly encourage you to ride to the races. Please drive slowly on Delwau Ln, respect the venue, their neighbors and be cognizant of bicycles and pedestrians.

Weather

The event is rain or shine. Delays or cancellations may be issued at the discretion of the promoter or race officials in the event of severe weather.

Producers

This event is produced by  Camp of Lamps LLC and Holland Racing LLC.

EventNotes:
Introducing the fall Adirondack Women's Weekend featuring two incredible days of fully supported road cycling from the relaxing and cozy Lodge at Schroon Lake.

Dates: October 9-11  
Location: Schroon Lake  
Mileage: 15-32 miles/day  
Participation Cap: 10 riders  
Benefits: Schroon Lake Association

Since the June Adirondack Women's Weekend sells out annually, it's time to introduce an intimate boutique event for the fall with a maximum of 10 riders. And there's no better place to host it than the stunning Schroon Lake region and the incredible Lodge at Schroon Lake. Whether attending solo or with friends, this small group experience is all about fun, relaxation and having a great time, on and off your bike. Add in delicious dining, fun surprises and the blissful ease of knowing everything is taken care of and you've got a weekend of enjoying the best of the southern Adirondacks without the stress of planning. We make sure of that by providing professional cycling guides, fully stocked rest stops, a mechanic, and a support vehicle.

Highlights include a delicious Friday arrival dinner, happy hours on Friday and Saturday, two incredible fully supported road cycling routes and the camaraderie you can only get from a small group tour in the Adirondacks.

Need a teaser? Check out this video from one of our June events in Saranac Lake, which we've modeled this new event after.

Best of all, a portion of the event proceeds will support the Schroon Lake Association and their volunteer efforts to preserve, promote, and protect the welfare of Schroon Lake, the Schroon River, and the watershed area.

Registration Includes

  • 2 nights’ single or double accommodations
  • 2 fully supported & guided road cycling routes
  • Hearty rest stops
  • Secure bike parking
  • Exquisite dinner the night of arrival
  • Breakfast Saturday and Sunday
  • Event gifts & surprises  
     

Our Host

Lodge at Schroon Lake

This incredible property is a beautiful 36-acre resort on the west shore of Schroon Lake featuring 116 rooms, 32 of which are pet-friendly. It includes hotel rooms, standalone cabins and chalets, and upscale glamping sites. Plus, guests have access to a world-class restaurant and bar, miniature golf, multi-purpose sports courts, and a private beach with docks and a deck. Additional amenities include an indoor pool, a private marina, a game room, and lawn games.

Pedal into Fall with us!

Don’t miss out — sign up, grab your shirt, and get ready to ride! 

PLEASE NOTE: Expect a calm, collaborative group environment where everyone moves forward together in a location that will be announced in the future. This is the first step of your adventure. Say yes, show up, and trust the ride—we’ll take care of the rest in a place worth exploring

Hassmer Fest 2026

Hassmer Fest is a three-day mountain bike festival is back for 2026! Enjoy the best mountain bike festival in Southeast Indiana.  Hassmer Fest is hosted within the beautiful Versailles State Park in Versailles, Indiana.  The trail system within the park offers miles of flowing single track, providing a great riding experience for all skill levels, from beginner to the most experienced. This year we celebrate thirteen years of the festival and nearly 30 miles of mountain trails. 

The park’s trail system exists due to the hard work and dedication of volunteers that have a love for mountain biking, as well as a love for the great outdoors.  Hundreds of volunteer hours are accrued each year to build and maintain the trail system.

All proceeds of Hassmer Fest go directly to support the efforts of the volunteer trail crew within Versailles State Park. Come out and enjoy a great weekend of riding, entertainment, and friendship.

Pre-Registration

Online Pre-Registration: $75.00 (March 1 - October 7, 2026)  

Day-of-Event Registration:  $90.00 - Cash, Check or Credit Card (via Square) at event site.

The Ride-em-All Challenge requires riders to ride nearly 30-miles of the trail system within Versailles State Park. 

Riders must ride with a punch card.  Punch cards can be claimed at registration area during the event. 

Ride-em-All signs are strategically placed on each of the trails within the mountain bike trail system. Each sign contains a unique orienteering punch.  Use the orienteering punch to mark your punch card accordingly.  

This is a pre-registration category only this year.  There is a fee of $20.00 to participate and receive your ride-em-all challenge hat. Please note this item a “trail” style hat from Cognative Mountain Biking. One size fits most!

You have some experience mountain biking and would like to increase your skills beyond the basics. This course will teach beginner-intermediate riders the technique to execute more efficient and controlled riding. This clinic is for those aged 14 and older.

 

Clinic Overview

This is a 2-hour clinic with optional on-trail practice following.

You’ll Learn:

October 10, 2026

Kids ages 6 and up who want to build the foundational skills of balance, confidence, and safety for fun and safe riding.

This is a 1 hour clinic.

You’ll Learn

  • Essentials for safe riding
  • Proper body position and maintaining balance while riding

EventName: Pumpkin Hop Cross 2026 - The Evolution of a SpeCXies
EventNotes:
NO RACING LICENSE IS REQUIRED TO ENTER & PARTICIPATE

All but the “first-timers” races require an entry fee.

Enter as many races for which you are qualified!  That means you can race within your category and higher, but not lower.  Races are gender-inclusive EXCEPT those designated "Women."  Those are...wait for it...just for the girls, but I'm not deciding for you what that means.  Juniors are not limited to the junior races.  Try those AND your category race if you want.  Just like single speed isn't limited to the single speed race.  Put that one-trick pony up against the geared machines in your category race and show 'em that gears don't mean a thang - it's cyclocross!  

Registration is online-preferred

Do this from any electronic, internet-equipped device you see fit, and that theoretically you own.  Use your preferred means of digital money, and voila!  You're in!  We can move stuff around on race-day or before if you need to make a change (see note on refunds below).  Let us know!  You can still register in person via Venmo or exact cash or check.  No set cut-off time before your race, but please be punctual and considerate of your registrar, official, and fellow racers.  The best way for all of us is online in advance. BikeReg closes at 4 p.m. Friday for the night race, then open for the rest of the weekend, AND you can register on site if your individual circumstance dictates. 

We plan to have the course open at 8:00 a.m. Saturday (7:00 on Sunday), with registration opening by 9:00 (8:00 on Sunday).  You'll likely use the same number all weekend, no matter the race.  This will depend, in part, on the number of registrants.

Licenses

NO RACING LICENSE REQUIRED.  This is not a USAC-sanctioned event this year.  We always hope more and more people get involved and it is an attempt at removing a potential barrier to entry.  Those of  you that do hold a license with USAC, keep up the good work!!!  Thank you, everyone, for your cyclocross ambassadorship!

Equipment

Run what you brung.  Ride what you can abide.  Bike what you like.  Wheel what you feel.  You do not have to have a cyclocross-specific steed.  You'll have a lot more fun if you at least have knobby tires, though.  That's pretty much a must.  As is a helmet.  We want you to have fun, but we need you to be safe, so you have to have a helmet and you have to wear it at all times while on your bike.

Staging & Starting Intervals

Staging is first-come, first-choice.  You know what time your race starts.  Just pay attention and play nice.  Yeah, we know you're strong and like that front row call up, but we also know you're going to be on the front before the hole shot, anyway.  You are a beast, after all.  Many of our races will have combined fields.  Our official(s) will determine the start time intervals and field order on race day.

Waivers

All participants or their parent/guardian (if under 18) must sign our waiver in-person at number pickup.

Podiums & Prizes

A podium presentation will occur as soon as possible following completion of each race.  Results typically are ready pretty quickly, so unless there is a protest - we've never had a protest; our officials are the tops - we'll get you called up for a picture and a prize post-haste.  We're awarding a total cash purse of an amount hopefully worth writing home about.  And it wouldn't be Pumpkin Hop Cross if we didn't give away a few pumpkins!

And pie.

RESULTS WILL BE UPLOADED TO CROSSRESULTS.COM

Refunds

Life happens.  Boy howdy, does it.  If you register, THANK YOU!!!  But then it turns out you can't come. If you want us to keep your money as a donation to the cause, THANK YOU!!!  If you would like to request a refund, THEN PLEASE DO!!!  We will miss you, absolutely, but you won't have to miss your cash for very long.  Sorry we can't refund BikeReg surcharges, though.  No refund requests will be considered after September 30th.

Rules

Our official(s) will be USA Cycling trained and experienced, so plan on abiding by USA Cycling rules. Check out usacycling.org if you need a review. Otherwise, be kind.  It supersedes all other rules, anyway.

CAMPING

When you register, please let us know if you’ll be camping with us, and if you will be pitching a tent or sleeping in your vehicle.  That will help us determine good locations for you and consider breakfast options, as well!  It is FREE to camp, of course.

WHAT DOES MY REGISTRATION COVER ?

Event insurance, rest stop food & drinks, advertising and logistics, and ride T-shirt.

A portion of your entry fee will benefit the Northern Neck Bike Club, a 501(c)3 nonprofit organization focused on building trails, mentoring youth, and empowering our community through cycling.

IS THERE A T-SHIRT FOR SALE?

Yes, each registrant will receive a T-shirt. You can purchase additional T-shirts for non-riding friends and family during registration.  

River Ride 2026 participants may also purchase a club-cut cycling jersey for $70 during registration.

Depending on size and quantity, T-shirts and jerseys purchased after Sept. 15 may be mailed to participants after the event.

THE ROUTES

The event will feature four course options: a 10-mile beginner/casual route, and main routes of 20, 29, 40 and 65 (metric century) miles. All routes wind through some of the most scenic and peaceful roads in Virginia’s Northern Neck.

RideWithGPS will be available to all participants, and the course will be marked with painted arrows before and after every turn. Preliminary maps are available here: River Ride 2026 Preliminary Routes. Final versions will be published the week prior to the event.

STOPS/TREATS/RIDE SUPPORT

Well-stocked rest stops will be available along the routes, each offering essential supplies and a warm, helpful team of volunteers.  Our SAG (Support and Gear) team will be monitoring the routes for your safety.

Afterwards, enjoy Kilmarnock’s Fall Festival at Town Centre Park.

AFTER-PARTY

The River Ride after-party will take place from 6-8 pm Saturday night at That Damn Mary Brewing Company (13 W Church St, Kilmarnock VA 22482). Your orange ride bracelet gets you access to the event. Additional guests can attend the party for a $5 cover (payable at the door if you didn't buy an extra at registration).

CAN I CHECK IN EARLY ?

Yes. We offer early check-in from 6:00pm–8:00pm on Friday, October 9 at Lancaster Elementary School.

WHEN CAN I CHECK IN ON RIDE DAY ?

Check-in opens at 6:30am at Lancaster Elementary School. Please park first, then come to the check-in table and pick up your t-shirt and rider packet. A ride concierge will be available answer questions about the routes and provide safety information. 

WHEN CAN I START THE RIDE?

Check-in opens at 6:30am and closes at 9:00 am.  

After checking in, riders depart at their own pace, but should plan their ride so they finish no later than 3:00pm. 

The last rest stop will close at 4:00pm.  Our support vehicles will sweep the course throughout the event day to ensure all riders return safely.

WHERE DO I PARK ?

Registration/Check-in/Main Ride: Please park at Lancaster Elementary School, or in the Town of Kilmarnock parking lot on the corner of West Church Street and School Street.

Beginner/Casual Ride: (Please check-in at Lancaster Elementary School before driving to the beginner/casual ride start). Park in the designated parking area at Shiloh School. Due to the heavy cycling traffic at this location, a volunteer will guide you to safely depart from the parking area when you have finished your ride.

ARE RESTROOMS AVAILABLE AT THE START? 

Yes, the elementary school has agreed to open restrooms during check-in and registration.  Additional port-a-potties will be provided, if needed.  

REFUNDS/DEFERRALS/TRANSFERS

As with most events of this caliber, there are no refunds. This is a rain or shine event. In the unlikely event that the ride must be canceled due to extreme weather (hurricanes, flooding, etc.), participants may receive credit toward registration for the make-up date, if scheduled, or toward the 2026 River Ride.

ARE E-BIKES ALLOWED?

Yes. Class 1 and Class 3 e-bikes are allowed because they are pedal-assisted.  Mopeds, scooters, and throttle-only e-bikes are not allowed.

ARE HELMETS REQUIRED ?

Yes.  An ANSI or SNELL certified helmet is required when riding a bike during this event.  All Virginia traffic laws must also be followed.

CAN MY YOUNG CHILDREN RIDE ALONG ?

River Ride 2026 includes a 10-mile beginner-friendly route that takes place on quiet farm roads; children under the age of 18 who participate in this route must be comfortable riding on open roads, and must be accompanied by a parent who must sign a waiver on their behalf. Children in baby seats or trailers are not permitted.

IS FOOD PROVIDED ?

Yes.  Every rest stop will be stocked with water and a variety of snacks. Also, the 20-, 29-, 40-, and 65-mile routes pass by convenience stores, farm markets, and agribusinesses that may be open on the day of the ride.

Riders planning to complete the metric century route should select a box lunch option during registration. That lunch will be ready for them at the lunch stop (Rice’s Hotel/Hughlett’s Tavern).

WHO DO I CONTACT IN CASE OF A CHALLENGE ALONG THE ROUTE ?

Because cell service can be limited, we strongly encourage riders to stay in groups.  If assistance is needed, call the number on your wristband at 804-480-2776.  Our team will locate and support you.  We also have volunteers and HAM radio operators driving the course to provide SAG support. If you need SAG support, please stay in a safe location along the route and watch for a SAG vehicle to come by.  

WHERE CAN I STAY OVERNIGHT ?

The Northern Neck has a wonderful variety of lodging options, from boutique hotels and waterfront rentals to world-class luxury lodging. Visit Virginia’s River Realm to learn more about lodging options for the ride weekend.

CAN I VOLUNTEER TO HELP?

Absolutely!  We’d love your support.  Please click here to contact the River Ride team directly.

The Filthy 50 is an annual gravel road cycling event that takes place on the gravel roads around Lanesboro, Minnesota on the second Saturday in October as the leaves on the trees begin to change. This is our 12th anniversary! There are 25 and 50 mile routes for our riders to choose from. All are welcome and encouraged. "Race it and set a record. Ride it and take in the beauty. Either way, get filthy." - Unknown

The Pretty Filthy 25 mile riders will leave downtown Lanesboro on Saturday, October 10th at 9:30am under police escort along with our 50 mile riders. They will follow the creek as they climb Grosbeak and Gentle eventually descending on Easy Street and then will turn south, following Gribben Creek out of the valley. After an epic return featuring Grit Road, it will be a hero’s welcome as they cross our finish line in the middle of downtown Lanesboro. This route features minimum maintenance roads, 1900+ feet of climbing, and some of the prettiest scenery you ever did see. If you haven’t attempted The Filthy before, we highly recommend that you start here.

The Filthy 50 mile riders will leave downtown Lanesboro on Saturday, October 10th at 9:30am under police escort, heading south and then east as they follow the creek climbing Grosbeak and Gentle then eventually descending on Easy Street. They will then climb the infamous Dew Drop and turn south towards “The Big Woods” and Amish country. These riders will want to consider their options when they reach Grub Hill and keep their wits about them when they hit the Amish maintained MMR just west of Henrytown. After making their way down Grit Road, crossing our finish line in downtown Lanesboro is gonna feel good. This route will feature several minimum maintenance roads, 3200+ feet of climbing, and perhaps a surprise or two along the way. It ain’t easy, but nothing worth doing ever is.

EventNotes:
Memphremagog Trails Present:  Grateful (An XC Race)

WE'RE SO BACK!

Welcome to Memphremagog Trails—quietly home to some of the best singletrack in the region. Once again home to Grateful, this XC mountain bike race is equally challenging and accessible at a fraction of the cost of typical cycling events!

 

The Course!

A freshly-updated 10-mile loop of pure singletrack magic:

  • Fast, flowy, machined descents
  • Tight, twisty tech (watch out for roots and tight trees…. It's old-school tech at its finest)
  • Over 1,300 ft of elevation gain per lap

Designed to challenge and reward riders of all levels.

 

Race It or Ride It!

You choose your vibe:

  • Race 1 Lap (10+ miles): A solid test of skill and stamina

  • Race 2 Laps (ENDURANCE….We like a little bit of crazy)

  • Party Pace Option: No timing —ride the course at your own speed, soak up the views. Enjoy the full race-day atmosphere without any pressure.

  • Kids Race/Ride: Free youth race/ride for new riders. Group leaders will lead the next generation through the youth course, ending at the same finish line as the racers. Adults should plan to ride with their kids.

Grateful is built on a “No Pressure, No Prejudice” mindset—welcoming all genders and abilities at an affordable cost.

 

The After-Party

After the ride, enjoy delicious local food trucks, live music, and the unbeatable energy of the Northeast Kingdom community. Local artisans will be at the on-site farmers market, and the pump track and skills area will be open to all ages. Bring the family and make a day of it.

 

2026 Cause

This year, Grateful will be recognizing our friend Anthony Moccia—co-founder of Rasputitsa and an early force behind Grateful, and a dedicated member of the Northeast Kingdom community. His leadership and generosity helped shape the inclusive riding culture we all value today.  

 

In his honor, proceeds from Grateful will support the Halo Foundation, which provides financial assistance to families navigating cancer treatment, and Little Bellas, an organization that creates a community to empower women through cycling

 

Our Story

Founded in 2021, Grateful has become a defining event in the Northeast Kingdom. Built on inclusion and connection, it brings together experienced riders and those new to the sport in a welcoming, challenging environment.

At its core, Grateful is about community. Through local partnerships and a commitment to giving back, the event has donated over $15,000 in the past five years to organizations that strengthen this place we call home.

 

Past and Future Events!

Want a sense of what to expect?  Check out this video! Curious about the course?  Here is the GPX file from 2025 (note…this course will be slightly different in 2026).

 

Interested in more XC racing in the NEK? Head over to Victory Hill and sign up for the Circumvictory! All Grateful participants get a special entry discount code!

About Kids Bike League

Kids Bike League is a program of the nonprofit Georgia Hi-Lo Trail, Inc. Our mission is to empower Georgia’s next generation of leaders through off-road cycling by fostering outdoor exploration, environmental stewardship, self-confidence, teamwork, and community engagement. Learn more at KidsBikeLeague.org.

Kids Bike League is committed to our belief that every child deserves the opportunity to explore outdoors, discover their potential, and connect with their community through the joy of cycling. All children are welcome at Kids Bike League regardless of their family’s ability to pay. For information about scholarship opportunities, contact Kids Bike League Director of Programming, Alden Strandburg.

Understanding Bikes & Gear

Kids Bike League supplies bikes and helmets to participants who do not have access to their own bike. 

Participants are welcome to bring their own bikes. Bikes must be in safe working order (brakes functioning, tires inflated, handlebars and seat secure). Coaches can help inspect bikes and provide alternatives when bikes are unsafe.

All participants are required to wear helmets when riding. Participants are also encouraged to bring helmets if available. Kids Bike League will provide helmets for participants when needed.

Preparing to Join a Ride

What to Wear

  • Wear comfortable clothing, with socks and closed-toed shoes.

What to Bring

  • Squeeze water bottles will fit bottle cages affixed to our bikes.
  • Sunscreen and insect repellent are highly recommended.
  • Bring medications necessary for allergies or other potential medical emergencies (e.g. inhalers, epinephrine) .

Ride Dates & Locations

  • A complete list of ride dates and locations is available on KidsBikeLeague.org.

EventNotes:
Can you Duro it? RIDE-TO and RIDE-AT 8 trail systems in one day? 60 miles of pavement & 40 miles of singletrack. 100 miles total. The FORC'n Duro is the ride of all MTB rides in the QC and probably one of the hardest days you'll have on a bike. Riders will be tested mentally and physically as they make their way from Dorrance Forest Preserve in Port Byron, IL to Westbrook Park in Dewitt, IA - while hitting tons of singletrack trails in between (Dorrance, Illiniwek, Sylvan Island, Sunderbruch, Scott Community College, Lost Grove Lake, Scott County Park and Westbrook Park); 100 miles in total. 

Not ready for the full 100 miles? Do the DIRT Duro and ride all trails in one day. 40+ miles of single track is a pretty respectable day!! Not in for the long haul? Join us anyway and ride what you want/can. A riders meeting will be held in the shelter at 6:50am where we will go over route cue sheets and other last-minute information. This ride is semi-supported. Bring tools, tubes, a pump, and any other gear you need to fix minor mechanical issues. A refuel station will be located at Healthy Habits a little past halfway and there are plenty of stores along the route to refill and refuel. 

**This year is more self-sufficient so bring the necessary tools and spares for a full day ride, and have a friend on call for bailing out if you have serious mechanical or other problems (ideally someone riding the Dirto who is likely nearby). 

-This year’s Route will include Scott Community College and a fun grass section around Lost Grove Lake on the way to Scott County Park. And exclude Stephens, Dog Park and Eldridge Rail Trail.

Rain date will be Saturday October 3rd. *** MUST BE A FORC MEMBER TO PARTICIPATE ***

The Triple Scoop has a single goal—to bring road, gravel, and mountain biking together into one race. It's a format unlike anything else in the Midwest, challenging riders to tackle all three disciplines in a single day... for FREE.

In its 5th year, the course covers (in order) approximately 30 miles of road, 25 miles of gravel, and 12–15 miles of singletrack (depending on course conditions).

In collaboration with the folks at Griffin Bike Park and the Vigo County Parks Department, this year's road and gravel routes have been refreshed, bringing new roads, new scenery, and a few new challenges. The mountain bike portion will once again feature a multi-lap format, showcasing Griffin Bike Park's unbelievable, hidden-gem trail system.

Solo racers will find the day to be a true test of endurance, versatility, and technical skill. While the distances may not look overwhelming on paper, putting all three disciplines together has proven to be a surprisingly difficult challenge, with many riders discovering that simply finishing the Triple Scoop is an accomplishment in itself. Some racers choose to ride a single bike all day (less advised), while others swap bikes in the transition area (more advised, with property kept under the watchful eye of the race directors and volunteers).

Relay teams experience the event from an entirely different perspective. Divide the disciplines among teammates, spend the day cheering each other on from the transition area, and enjoy one of the most unique team events on the cycling calendar. Whether you're racing for the podium or just sharing a memorable day on bikes, the relay format has become a favorite for good reason.

How you decide to tackle the race is up to you. If you're looking for a late-season physical challenge, enter solo and see how you stack up. If you'd rather celebrate everything that makes cycling great, gather a team, bring a pop-up tent, and spend the day with us.

Carpool if at all possible. We will be using a large portion of the parking lot as our transition/finish line village (details below), so parking will be somewhat limited.

 

Routes (in order): 

1. Road route (~30 miles): TBD - updated by September 1, 2026

2. Gravel route (~25 miles): TBD - updated by September 1, 2026

3. MTB route: 2 laps of https://www.strava.com/routes/3255178681813258410 

 

Transition Village: 

 

The transition village is perhaps the most exciting non-racing element of the race. All racers, crew, and spectators will be stationed in a celebratory “tunnel” of team tents that mark the start and end of each leg of the race (see "Common FAQs #3 for the race start exception). 

 

All racers will “pass” through the transition village/finish line between each leg. For solo riders, this is done to change bikes or for time checkpoints. For relay teams the finish line is the location for the “baton pass." This will also be the finish line for the entire race. Fingers crossed for a sprint finish!

 

We’d like to see as many teams and solo racers as possible bring out a pop up tent, umbrellas, chairs, coolers, etc. Whether you come bare bones or full-festival mode, you’ll be assigned a spot along the “transition village” to be your official transition zone. 

 

Race Notes/Event Philosophy:


The Race Is Still Free

The Triple Scoop will once again be a free race. At this point, it's become part of who we are.

Several racers have asked what they could do with the race entry fee they would normally expect to pay. If that's you, we'd encourage you to consider supporting one (or both) of the organizations that help make this event possible.

Support Griffin Bike Park

Griffin Bike Park generously allows us to take over their trails and parking lot on race day at no cost. Beyond that, the Friends of Griffin Bike Park volunteer countless hours helping with course marking, timing, setup, and cleanup. If you'd like to give back to the people who make this race possible, consider making a donation here:

https://griffinbikepark.com/cash-donation/

Support World Bicycle Relief – Indiana

The Indiana chapter of World Bicycle Relief is another organization we're proud to support. Their work helps provide life-changing transportation through bicycles around the world.

You can donate here:

https://www.powerofbicycles.org/fundraisers/wbrindiana

Stickers = Race Support

I'll once again have Triple Scoop stickers available on race day for $5 each.

People occasionally ask what it costs to put on a free race. I'm always happy to talk about it—I actually think the numbers are encouraging, because they show that with enough resourcefulness, almost anyone could organize something like this.

After race expenses are covered, every remaining dollar from sticker sales will be split evenly between Griffin Bike Park and World Bicycle Relief. Full nonprofit race mode.

Camp the Night Before

The last two years, my family and I have camped at Fowler Park, directly across the road from Griffin Bike Park, and we've had a fantastic time. We'll be doing it again this year.

If you're interested in arriving Friday evening, we'd love to have a casual campfire hangout with anyone who wants to join us. Whether you're in a tent or camper, it's a great way to kick off the weekend before race day.

Camping reservations can be made here:

https://www.campspot.com/book/fowlerparkin

 

Common FAQs:

 

0. (So common it doesn't even get a number) Can I just ride my very capable gravel bike for the whole race?

- Yes. However, we assure you that the mountain bike route carefully curates the best trails in Griffin Bike Park that highlight PURE mountain biking. Trails incorporated into a gravel race course are awesome - but these trails are not the same as those. Saying all that - run what you brung, and if you have to walk a couple sections just be sure you aren't holding up your fellow racers.

 

1. Can I use aero bars/a TT bike for the road portion?

- Yes, do whatever it takes to be as fast as possible. Heck, you can use a TT bike for the trails if you want. It’s your body. 

 

2. I’m signing up as a team. Can I do 2 of the legs but grab a teammate for the 3rd?

- Yes. Viable teams are 2-3 members. The 3 legs of the race must be completed in the correct order (road, gravel, mtb) and the same “pass” through the transition village is still required even for those who are completing two legs in a row on the same bike.

 

3. Do I have to ride my road bike from that gravel parking lot?!

- Nah. Road is the FIRST leg of the race with the start line at the park entrance to make for a more positive start for the road riders. The only downside to this is when you finish the road leg of the race, you’ll either be riding or running your road bike up to the official transition area. Gravel and MTB legs of the race will start and finish at the official transition village. So far, we have seen ZERO flats in 4 years from the roadies that opt to ride their bike up and all the way through the transition village.

 

4. I'm going to sign up as part of a relay team. Do my teammates need to fill out this form too?

- Yes. The primary purpose of the sign up form is to count how many total participants to expect and to take care of liabilities/rider safety details at a free race. Each team member needs to be submitted as a separate sign up and share the same team name - if there are errors, we will take care of combining you in the data sheet on the back end. You can always email joel.e.karl@gmail.com.

 

6. Will there be SAG/water/nutrition at the transition?

- As this is a free event, plan on this being self-supported in every way. Last year, we did position a support volunteer at the “wildest” point of the gravel course. However, the nature of the race coming back to the same parking lot lends to a normal distance between aid stations at any other race. We’ll be looking for support once we have a firm grasp on early participants, but plan to bring your own nutrition. We will have large jugs of water at the transition area.

 

7. Will there be a prize?

- No cash prizes of any kind. We've enjoyed a variety of trophies over the years; Epic laser-cut trophies and etched mini-growlers being the most recent. Trophies will be awarded for the podium in each category (open solo, women’s solo, open team, women’s team, nonbinary solo, nonbinary team).

 

8. Can I bring my friends and family to watch? 

- Absolutely! Griffin Bike Park is the perfect venue for the whole family to enjoy bike-centric fun. Every year, there's a great, family-friendly energy of kids and adults riding the pump tracks and jump lines right next to the parking lot. Warm up by riding down the dual slalom course. Stay tuned for more things to do before, during, and after the race.

 

10. If I'm doing the whole Triple Scoop solo, how will my bikes be kept safe while I'm out riding?

- There will always be people present at the transition village. Race directors and racers waiting for their turn in the race will provide ample protection through “positive peer pressure”, and the parking lot is very shielded in view from any road traffic (very little) that might drive by.

 

11. If I'm on a team, what do I do while I'm waiting for my turn?

- Bring a lawn chair, some food, music, drinks, etc! Ride the pump tracks and jump lines right next to the parking lot. Race down the dual slalom course.

 

12. Can I be on multiple teams? Like, bro, just imagine, if I could blow up the field on the road leg, then switch teams and ride gravel, probably try to blow that up too… then my original team's mountain biker would be able to crush all the solo guys!
- You can only sign up for one team (Paul).

EventNotes:
Ride to Support 
Housing. Health. Hope.

 

A RIDE WITH A PURPOSE 
SINCE 1993

What began as a small community Bikeathon in 1993 has grown into a tradition of hope, compassion, and community. For more than 30 years, every ride has helped The Center in Asbury Park provide Housing, Health, & Hope by connecting people with safe housing, access to healthcare, nutritious meals, recovery support, and other essential services that help rebuild lives.

More than three decades later, the legacy rides on with three routes for every level of cyclist—from casual riders looking for a fun day through Asbury Park to seasoned enthusiasts seeking a greater challenge up the Jersey shoreline. Each route offers beautiful coastal scenery, great camaraderie, and the opportunity to make a real difference. 

Every mile ridden helps open the door to a brighter future. Join us and be part of a tradition that has been changing lives and creating change in our community.

Brazen Dropouts Cycling Team is excited to invite everyone to the inaugural Englewood CX Race at the Englewood Farm in Fall River, WI! The farm is located ~45 minutes northeast of downtown Madison, and it is a excellent  location for a CX race! Need venue palmares? Englewood has hosted WORS, NICA, and UCI mountain bike races! The farm has natural terrain and trails that make for an incredibly fun and challenging (this is ‘cross afterall) CX course! We’re talkin’ FAST “Hay Bale Switchbacks™”, we’re talkin’ challenging climbs, and we’re talkin’ features that hearken back to the OG BD SP (who’s with me still?) course, BERMS! That’s right, the “rollercoaster on a bike” feeling that we’ve missed since Sheehan gave us the boot is BACK! Bring your friends, family, and anyone who likes to have a good time out to the farm for an amazing day of fun and fast racing!

As you are visiting a working farm, there are a few rules that we ask you follow:

 

Leave the livestock alone, and don’t open any gates. Also, please don’t touch the fences, they will shock you. 

 

No Pets. For the safety of everyone involved, we ask that you leave your dogs, cats, birds, snakes, and ferrets at home. Goldfish are fine.

 

No glass bottles. Broken glass is dangerous to cattle and very hard to clean up. 

 

Please properly dispose of any gel packs as cattle love sugar and electrolytes too, and the plastic is very dangerous to their digestive tracts.

 

Please stay out of the deer stands.

 

Use the field entrance the the east of the house driveway (it’ll be well marked).

 

Be Nice, ride bikes, have fun!

EventName: CLEVELAND Cycling Academy TALENT ID CAMP Fueled by Hammer Nutrition
EventNotes:
2027 JUNIOR TALENT ID CAMP FUELED by HAMMER NUTRITION


2-Day Performance Development Camp on October 10th & 11th


Led by CCA's U23 Team Members: Judah Thompson and Nico Haydar

Note: All participants will receive camp water bottles and daily nutrition from product partner, Hammer Nutrition, during the scheduled camp rides.

PURPOSE
Identify high-potential riders for CCA and give juniors a taste of performance development. We want riders to learn skills they can use in both training and racing, including group riding, bike handling, positioning, race tactics, and how to approach their overall development as cyclists through basic training methods, nutrition, recovery, and healthy habits.

The camp will also focus on building confidence. A lot of young riders are still learning how to ride safely and comfortably in a group, move through a field, make decisions during a race, and understand what they should be doing during different parts of a race. We want to give them the opportunity to learn these things in a controlled environment before putting them into a race.

Another goal is to build a strong junior cycling community. We want riders from different teams and backgrounds to spend time together, learn from each other, and build relationships with other juniors who are serious about riding and racing.

The camp is not only about finding the strongest rider. We want to identify riders who show potential, a willingness to learn, good bike skills, race awareness, competitiveness, and the ability to respond to feedback. We are looking for riders who are coachable and have the potential to continue developing.

Most importantly, we want juniors to leave the camp loving riding their bikes, feeling more confident on the bike, and excited to race and continue improving. The goal is to identify potential riders for CCA while also giving every rider something they can carry with them during the cycling journey.
 

5 PILLARS OF TALENT ID
1.    Physical Potential: Power, aerobic fitness, sprint, repeatability
2.    Race Ability: Positioning, tactics, decision-making
3.    Bike Skills: Pack skills, comfort on the bike, cornering
4.    Coachability: Listens, adapts, asks questions, responds to feedback
5.    Character: communication, work ethic, resilience, good team behavior
 

What we are looking for
The camp is not only about finding the strongest rider. We want riders who are in tune with the race, willing to learn, respond well to feedback, and contribute positively to the group. A strong team rider should communicate, support others, and lift the riders around them.

 

DAY 1 — THE FOUNDATION

Day 1 will focus on sprint testing, education, and group riding. Riders will start with sprint testing to assess short-duration power, followed by an education session covering pack skills, basic training methods, nutrition, recovery, and overall development as a cyclist. After lunch, the focus will shift to group riding and bike skills, teaching riders how to ride safely and confidently in a group, communicate, hold their position, and move through the group. The group ride is planned as a 30–60 mile coached ride with a follow vehicle.

SPRINT TESTING
The sprint test will give us a simple measure of each rider’s ability to produce power. Riders will complete a maximum 5-second sprint followed by a maximum 30-second effort. This gives us a look at both explosive power and the ability to sustain a high-power effort beyond the initial sprint. The test can be done using a bike set up on a Wahoo KICKR, allowing us to consistently record each rider’s power. Riders will have two opportunities to complete each effort, with adequate recovery between attempts. The first attempt also gives riders a chance to understand the setup and pacing before their second attempt.

CLASSROOM SESSION
The classroom session will introduce juniors to the basics of performance development and what it takes to become a better cyclist. Topics will include pack skills, basic training methods, how to structure training, nutrition and fueling, recovery, and preparation for racing. The goal is to give riders practical knowledge they can take back to their own training and use throughout the season.

GROUP RIDE + BIKE SKILLS
The group ride will focus on developing the skills and confidence needed to ride safely and effectively in a group. Riders will work on holding a wheel, maintaining their line, communication, positioning, moving through the group, pacelines, and responding to changes in speed. Coaches will introduce basic race situations throughout the ride so riders can practice these skills before the race simulations on Day 2.


DAY 1  TAKEAWAY
Riders leave with a better understanding of their physical ability, stronger pack skills, and practical knowledge about training, nutrition, recovery, and racing.

 

DAY 2 — RACE SIMULATION

Day 2  will focus on applying the skills and knowledge from Day 1 in a race environment. Riders will take part in race simulations designed to test positioning, decision-making, race awareness, team tactics, competitiveness, and their ability to respond to changing situations. This will allow us to observe how riders use the skills they learned, communicate with others, respond to attacks, manage their effort, and make decisions under pressure. The race simulations will also give riders the opportunity to experience a race environment and build confidence competing with other juniors.

COURSE PREVIEW
Before racing, riders will preview the course and go over the key points they need to be aware of during the race. This will include the finish, climbs, wind direction, technical sections, sprint or KOM/QOM points, and overall race safety. The goal is to help riders understand the course and identify where different race situations could develop.

RACE SIM #1 — NO TEAMS
Riders will compete in a 20–25 km race simulation designed to create a realistic racing environment. The race will include attacks, sprint opportunities, breakaway opportunities, and technical sections, with the potential for KOM/QOM points. Riders will race individually, allowing coaches to observe how they naturally position themselves, read the race, and make decisions without a team strategy.

POST-RACE DEBRIEF
After the race, riders will discuss what they saw and how they approached the race. Coaches will ask what they tried to do, why they made certain decisions, and what they would do differently. This will give coaches a better understanding of each rider’s race awareness, decision-making, and race IQ beyond their finishing position.

RACE SIM #2 — TEAM ENVIRONMENT
The second race simulation will place riders into a team environment with assigned roles, such as sprinter, climber, breakaway rider, or domestique. Each team will be given a tactical objective to execute during the race. This will allow coaches to see how riders communicate, work together, respond to the race, and apply the skills learned on Day 1 and in Race Sim #1 under pressure and in a team environment.
 

DAY 2  TAKEAWAY
Riders apply what they learned, experience a competitive race environment, and receive feedback on their decision-making, race awareness, and team behavior.

 

PROPOSED CAMP FLOW

  • DAY 1

    • THE FOUNDATION: Sprint Testing • Education • Group Riding • Bike Skills

  • DAY 2 

    • RACE SIMULATION: Course Preview • Individual Race • Debrief • Team Race

EventName: Great River Ride Century / Berkshire Brevets 2026
EventNotes:
Great River Ride 2026

A Fundraiser for the Friends of the Columbia Greenway Rail Trail Inc.

Post Ride Entertainment and Buffet at the finish

2026 marks the 39th Anniversary of the Great River Ride. Over the years the GRR has been recognized by the League of American Bicyclists (LAB) and Bicycling Magazine as one of the top century rides in America. A variety of routes are offered to match the skill levels of all participants. Event proceeds will benefit the programs of the Friends of the Columbia Greenway Rail Trail (FOCGRT), a 501 3c nonprofit organization.  

Staffed refreshment stops along the ride as well as a post-ride buffet with live entertainment from 2:00 PM to 5:30 PM. 

You will encounter knee-popping hills, breathtaking views, awesome descents, and gorgeous fall foliage as you tour the hilltowns of the Eastern Berkshires. Add in miles of stone walls, waterfalls, plenty of New England white churches, loads of colonial homes, historic keystone arches, a wild and scenic river, and did I mention hills. But thats not all, we've got rest stops staffed with friendly cyclists and snacks, including our famous "Baked Potato" stop.

The Westfield River, the Great River in the river ride, is a federally designated Wild and Scenic River. The GRR wanders the course of this scenic river to give you a unique cycling experience. For 2026 we're using most of the original route, thanks to Mass Highways repaving projects. 

The GRR Gravel Route is a mix of pavement, gravel, dirt and seasonal roads that we’ve enjoyed fall riding on for over 50 years. The 72 mile route is 40% unpaved..  The route will take you through the remote Knightville Basin and Chesterfield Gorge with stunning vistas along the East Branch of the Westfield River. You’ll pass through the Knightville Meadows, the Rainbow Pool, the Little Gorge and the Chesterfield Gorge on your ride.  Most climbs are paved but Thayer Rd. is a moderately difficult climb of 1.4 miles on dirt ranging from 10% to 7%.  A long descent to River Rd. follows a seasonal road with some steep downgrades. At River Rd. you will have a choice of the final gravel climb up Maynard Rd. or the bailout paved climb up East River Hill to the Spud stop at the Chester Hill Church. Gravel/Dirt sections will not be monitored by SAG vehicles and Cell Phone coverage is limited.  Be prepared to handle mechanical problems,and flats.  Several miles of the route follows a gated road closed to motor vehicles.   We recommend teaming up with other riders on these sections.  Tire widths of 38mm or wider are recommended.  Fallen leaves will hide loose and bony surfaces, so caution on descents is advised.

Our Winery Ride uses the Columbia Greenway Rail Trail and New Haven/Northampton Canal Trail for a flat 28 mile ride with a stop at the Brignole Vineyard for snacks (wine will be available for purchase).

Our 42 mile road route includes one moderate climb up the Granville Gorge with a mid ride rest stop at the Brignole Vineyard. At the vineyard you will have the choice of returning on the road (rolling terrain) or using the rail trail (flat).

The 25 mile route will give you a taste of the area's hills. While there is no mid-point rest stop on this route, you will be able to visit the Granville Harvest Festival mid-way through the ride. Visit craft booths, sample local Mead and take a break before heading back to the finish party.

Family Friendly - Free entry for children 15 & under riding with a registered adult.

Riders choosing to ride the RUSA sanctioned 200K must be current RUSA members and are expected to comply with RUSA Randonneuring Rules and the official start times for their respective event.

             The RUSA  Brevet and Populaires options are a timed events. A Poulaire is a timed long distance event of less than 200K while a brevet is 200K or greater conducted under the rules of the Adaux Club Parisien and its American counterpart, Randonneurs USA. Like a Gran Fondo pace line riding is permitted and there is an upper time limit for finishing. Brevet and Populaire riders cannot start before the posted start time. The clock start at the posted start time for each ride, no adjustments are made for late starts. All brevet and populaire riders are issued a route card that must be signed/stamped at each control (rest stop). Completed cards must be signed and handed in at the finish. The RUSA  (Randonneurs USA) Brevet and Populaire are timed with a 6:00 AM start time for the 200K ride. No adjustments are made for late starts and all finishers must turn in a completed ride passport at the end of the ride to have a time recorded. 200K Brevet riders are required to have lights (front and rear), a reflective vest and reflective ankle bands. 

The Great River Ride benefits the Bicycle Advocacy efforts of New Horizons Bikes and the Friends of the Columbia Greenway Rail Trail.

Friends of the Columbia Greenway Rail Trail exists to ensure that the Columbia Greenway project is realized.  Specifically, Friends of the Columbia Greenway Rail Trail (FOCGRT) will advocate for the planning, design, construction, maintenance and continuance to the Columbia Greenway Rail Trail, as well as advocating for cycling improvements to make Westfield a bicycle friendly community.

 This is a Rain or Shine Event: No refunds
PresentedBy: Friends of the Columbia Greenway Rail Trail Inc. & New Horizons Bikes

EventNotes:
Welcome to the 5th annual Green Mountain Cyclocross! Racing will be on Sunday, October 11th. We will also have 2 free skills clinics on Saturday, October 10th. This event is run by Green Mountain Off-Road, a 501(c)(3) non-profit, and in partnership with the Catamount Outdoor Family Center. Proceeds from the race will help support the GMCX development race team, Catamount's youth programs, as well as other local youth cycling organizations and racing endeavors. We look forward to welcoming you to northern Vermont at the most scenic race venue in the history of New England cyclocross. Scroll for some details below.

 

RACE LICENSES:  GMCX is sanctioned under North American Bicycle Racing Association (NABRA). No membership or annual licenses are required. There is NO requirement for a USA Cycling license. JUST SHOW UP AND RACE!

 

DAY-OF REGISTRATION IS AVAILABLE FOR A $10 LATE FEE. CASH, CHECK, VENMO ACCEPTED.

 

ALL JUNIOR RACES ARE FREE thanks to generous support from Nick Depasquale Photography.

 

REGISTER FOR A SECOND RACE FOR $20!

 

VOLUNTEER SIGN UP HERE!

 

CAMPING: There will be limited camping spots available on-site Saturday night. You can purchase camp spots on the registration page under “merchandise”. Cost is $20 per adult.

 

PARKING: Parking at COFC is tight, please follow our volunteer parking attendant’s expert flag waving and pointing. Parking is NOT permitted on the south side of Governor Chittenden Road. Overflow parking is located at the ‘Oval’ on the north side of the road just before you reach the Catamount Outdoor Center. 

 

THERE ARE NO PETS ALLOWED AT THE CATAMOUNT OUTDOOR CENTER - We know, your dog is goodest of all the good dogs, but please leave that beast at home. We appreciate you respecting this rule of our gracious hosts Catamount Outdoor Family Center. 

 

THE COURSE: Our course consists of an approximately 1.6 mile lap that includes a mix of fun and technical turns, punchy climbs, and longer power sections. The course includes several dismounts. We expect the fastest riders to cover the lap in about 6.5 minutes. Expect baller views.

 

PRE-RIDING: There is NO course pre-riding during a race. To pre-ride, ONLY enter the course BEYOND the start/finish line when the official confirms that the last rider of the current race has begun their last lap. DO NOT PASS anyone still racing. Failure to do so will result in disqualification. 


STAGING: Staging for each race will occur 10 minutes before the designated start time. Staging will be by order of CrossResults ranking, followed by day-of registration.

 

CLUB ROW: The GMCX course is just across the road from the parking areas. You can purchase a 10X10 pop-up tent space for your team next to the course. Spaces are limited, so reserve yours early!

 

FOOD AND DRINK: Frost Beer Works will be on site slinging brews from 12:15 to 4:15. GMCX volunteers will be grilling burgers, veggie burgers, and dogs for purchase, and we will have cold seltzers and sodas. We will have apples and cider donuts for suggested donation of 50 cents per apple, and $2.00 per donut. 

 

SKILLS CLINICS: with the goal of increasing participation numbers of WGD* and junior athletes, we are offering 2 skills clinics on Saturday, October 10th. One will be geared toward junior racers, and the other for WGD athletes and they will be instructed by former World Cup athletes and local pros. Clinics will be tailored for novice to intermediate skill levels. Each clinic will be capped at 20 riders, with spots reserved for individuals who identify as Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC) participants. Clinic check-in will be at the Catamount Outdoor Family Center starting at 2:00 PM, and the clinics will start at 3:00. Don't have a cyclocross bike? That's ok! Your gravel bike or hardtail mountain bike is good enough to get you started!

 

THE VENUE: The Catamount Outdoor Family Center (COFC) is in Williston, Vermont, just outside of Burlington, with beautiful views of the Green Mountains. COFC began as a cross country ski center in 1978. It quickly expanded to include mountain bike and trail running, and now also hosts a variety of youth outdoor and educational programming. It has a rich history of hosting local, regional, and international level bike racing, including UCI cyclocross and mountain bike events. Racing GMCX will directly support Catamount's ongoing outdoor efforts!

New England's Fall Classic, the Lime Rock Park Epic

Based at the legendary Lime Rock Park in Connecticut's Litchfield County, this gravel fondo showcasing waterfalls and covered bridges has emerged as an autumn classic in the Berkshires. Perhaps the most beautiful ride in the region, this course and format are welcoming to riders of most abilities on a proper bike. For those who want to go hard, the timed segments will challenge them. For those looking for a nice fall tour, these roads will enrapture you…especially given the fall foliage that peaks earlier than the rest of New England.

 All riders will start and finish on the fabled raceway near the Sam Posey Bridge, complete a lap on the raceway and then exit the venue.  Riders will be offered three distances: The Epic (70 miles), the Explorer (55 miles) and the Express (25 miles). The Epic and Explorer will feature chip timed segments. Cumulative times across multiple segments will be compared for podium places. All riders will receive a meal and drink ticket for the post-ride celebration.

RETURNING FOR 2026: 5K Running Race to Support the Hole in the Wall Gang Camp.  After the gravel riders depart the venue for the Epic and Explorer routes, organizers will host a 5k running/walking event on the fabled Lime Rock Park racetrack. To find out about that, click HERE. 

VOLUNTEER OPPORTUNITIES. Riders seeking discounted or comp entries may be able to provide volunteer service in exchange for such discounts. Parents of juniors are encouraged to do so. Contact Richard@DomestiqueEvents.com for more information. 

PINK PATROL DOMESTIQUES WANTED!  Would you like to ride the event and help out with getting differing levels of riders to the finish for a deep discount as part of our Pink Patrol?  If so, come join our team and help make someone's experience better along the way.  Domestiques are welcome and encouraged to ride at their own pace in the timed segments and will be considered for awards, if so desired. To be considered for this exciting opportunity to contribute, contact Richard@DomestiqueEvents.com for more information. 

ENTRY DEFERMENT POLICY: While Domestique Events DOES NOT OFFER REFUNDS for any reason, organizers will allow entrants to either transfer their entry in the Lime Rock Park Epic to another person OR defer the entry to the 2027 Natchaug Epic being held March 27. Entries may only be deferred one time. The deadline to do so is 11:59 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 5. To request a deferment and/or transfer send email to admin@DomestiqueEvents.com. 

The Routes

THE EPIC

70 miles, 5,200 ft of elevation, 20 sectors, 5 timed segments, 2 rest stops

If Ralph Lauren could design a bike ride, this might just be the product. With road names "Wildcat Hollow," "Dark Hollow", “Old Asylum,” and "Race Track," we knew that Paul and Bob found some good stuff for our course. And that's all BEFORE Rest Stop 1. The Epic will send riders north by The Great Falls along the Housatonic River before cutting "Between the Lakes." The route turns south and carries riders through several rolling gravel sectors to Sharon. Then we truly make it epic. A 3.3-mile gravel climb sets the tone before the long haulers whistle down a seven-mile "pedalers" descent, 3.5 of which is un-paved. The course offers some autumnal heaven along the river before spooning out a taste of hell: a 3-mile climb, most of which is unpaved, forces riders to grind out of the valley. The best of riders will be technically, aerobically and spiritually challenged. Regroup and recover at the top. The second rest stop, positioned in a classic Grange Hall converted into a fire house.  From there, a rider gets to celebrate a series of blissful ridges, eye-watering descents, scenic farmlands, a new challenging timed segment on Jeep track before dropping down to the covered bridge in West Cornwall. The final timed segment will be on the Lime Rock raceway and Rattlesnake Ridge in the opposite direction. Then come home to an amazing meal, friends and stories of the day with some cold ones. 

NOTE: Epic riders are eligible for the team-based Berkshire Cup competition. (Details below) 

THE EXPLORER

55 miles, 3700 ft of elevation, 14 sectors, 4 timed segments, 2 rest stops

The Explorer is comprised of the northern loop of the Epic route. The first half is fairly flat with the same gravel sectors.  After the rest stop the challenging stuff really starts, with a 4.5-mile gravel step climb. This route provides riders a good taste of the Epic without suffering the agony of the Epic's descent into the infernal Kent Valley. The Explorer riders reconnect with the Epic route and enjoy the second rest stop together. Be warned, this route is truly a challenge for even an accomplished rider. 

NOTE: PEDAL-ASSISTED E-BIKES ARE WELCOMED ON THE EXPLORER RIDE (but are EXCLUDED from any timed competitions).

THE EXPRESS

25 miles, 1000 ft of elevation, 5 sectors, no timed segments, lots of snack stops and clinics

The Express offers an approachable route for the "gravel curious." There are five unpaved sectors, three of which offer paved “bailouts.”  The Pink Patrol, comprised of experienced ride leaders, will divide up the group based on skills and experience. While some will take on the challenging Mount Easter Loops, others may stay on the paved route for the “tap-out” option to the covered bridge. From there we will descend down to the picturesque West Cornwall Covered Bridge. There the route turns north to traverse the third unpaved sector of the ride, a flat three miles along the Housatonic River. Five miles of rolling roads with a photo stop and snacks at the Great Falls will bring you back to Lime Rock Park.

NOTE: PEDAL-ASSISTED E-BIKES ARE WELCOMED ON THE EXPRESS RIDE. 

The Express will feature five unpaved sectors; approximately one fourth of the route is unpaved. There will be frequent photo stops with snacks. Riders will be timed but not scored. 

THE BERKSHIRE CUP TEAM COMPETITION
 
There will be a team competition. To be eligible each member must register with their team affiliation. Team membership will be determined based on the 'Team/Club/Company' field during BikeReg checkout. Please ensure all team members use the same name for your team.
 
Rules are as follows: 
  • There are two categories: Men and Women.
  • Men must have a minimum of four riders; women must have a minimum of three riders.
  • There is no maximum number of riders one team can have.
  • Only riders who enter and complete the Epic course and all five timed segments by 3 p.m. will be scored
  • Only the time of the fourth best rider of each men's team in each segment will be used for scoring. The aggregate of those scores will be tabulated for the team's result.
  • Only the time of the third best rider of each women's team in each segment will be used for scoring. The aggregate of those scores will be tabulated for the team's result.
  • Any combination of riders on a team can be scored. For example, a team may have different riders scored in each of the segments.
  • The overall individual results have no bearing on the team competition.
  • Only one men's and one women's team will be awarded the Berkshire Cup. 

ENTRANTS TO RECEIVE

All paid entrants to the Lime Rock Park Epic will receive the following: 

  • Free parking
  • Pre-ride mechanical support
  • SAG service
  • Rolling mechanical support courtesy of Speed and Sprocket and Comp Edge
  • Fully stocked rest stops featuring homemade and locally sourced food. Vegan and gluten free offerings made with love and affection.
  • One post ride meal featuring a chef prepared buffet featuring gluten free, vegetarian, and vegan offerings
  • One drink ticket to enjoy a cold brew or soft drink.
  • One amazing course with chip timing services provided by Holeshot Events.
  • Souvenir pint glass.
  • Awards presentation for the combined timed segments go to the top three Epic finishers in Open Men, Open Women, Men 45-plus, and Women 45-plus divisions.
    • *If a participant places in both the Open and 45-plus Categories, they will get the higher placing in the appropriate Category and be ineligible for awards in the other.  (i.e. - No double-dipping on the awards.)
  • Awards presentation for the combined timed segments go to the top Explorer finisher in Open Men, Open Women, Men 45-plus, and Women 45-plus divisions.
    • *If a participant wins in both the Open and 45-plus Categories, they will get the higher placing in the appropriate Category and be ineligible for awards in the other.  (i.e. - No double-dipping on the awards.)

About the Quick Six

EventNotes:
The 3rd Annual Crooked River Rambler is here! Join us for a proper Western Maine gravel adventure at peak fall foliage! Explore the most beautiful gravel roads and quirky rural delights that the Crooked River watershed has in store…and have fun doin' it! 

 

What's new for 2026

  • The same great route (if it's not broke…)
  • For those who want to keep on Ramblin', a new 10-mile "Crooked-Kezar Extension" is on offer, details below
  • To pile on this year's Kezar love, we're adding a new community partner, the Greater Lovell Land Trust!
  • A friggin' rad new Crooky logo and t-shirt courtesy of our friend and amazing local artist, Amy Borch
  • And the snacks keep getting better! 

The Highlights

  • Pedal by half a dozen remote ponds in a lush Maine pine forest
  • Soak in epic mountain views from your high gravel perch
  • Conquer historic farm roads and ATV trails
  • Ponder the mythical “Hand on the Rock”  
  • Gaze into the depths of the legendary Kezar Gorge 

This ride is not a race. It's designed to bring people together around a shared love of the outdoors and provide an opportunity to challenge yourself, explore a new place, and hopefully make a few new friends! Read on for more specifics, but know this: the route is mostly sane, at times a lil' chunky, and may make you laugh (hopefully not cry, but no promises). 

Rules 

  1. Be safe
  2. Have fun
  3. Get shit done
  4. Don't take yourself too seriously

What's included in my registration fee: 

  • Parking for the ride
  • Free Camping
  • A sweet “Crooked River Rambler” sticker
  • Post-ride meal (with options for all diets) provided by the wonderful Franck's Foods 

Venue 

This event will take place at Headwaters Basecamp, a new rural recreation hub in the foothills of the White Mountains and high in the Crooked River headwaters region. Everything before and after the ride will take place at this location. Here there will be a check-in tent, water, porto-potties, and food (coffee and baked goods before the ride, food truck after the ride). This is also where you will park for the event, and stick around for the afterparty (more below)! 

The Ride 

  • 10am start, don't be late! (Check-in starts at 9am)
  • 3 Aid-Stations with yummy snacks, water, and enthusiastic dancing fishes
  • The OG Crooky route is 33 miles, 65% off pavement, and a hell of a lot of fun. Checkout the full route here. There is also strategic shortcut at the halfway mark for those who'd prefer a shorter (23 miles) ride. This is the bizzness!
  • If you're one of those crazies who wants more…
  • New this year: The “Crooked-Kezar Extension": An optional 10-mile addition that brings you further into the Kezar River watershed then loops you on back to the OG Crooky Route to finish off your ride back to Headwaters. This extension is for those piddle-pedalers who want to keep on pushin', blasting you on up to the finest hill country general store there ever was: the Center Lovell Market. Enjoy the Baldface views and a sneaky cute antique shop, then send it back down to the Kezar River valley floor and bring ‘er on home. Here's the route plus the extension.

Recommended Bike/Gear 

  • All riders should be prepared and self-sufficient! Bring spare tube, pump/c02, patch kit, tire irons, repair tool.
  • Bring plenty of water storage capacity and snacks. Distances between water re-fill and snack stations may be up to 15 miles.
  • It is recommended you ride this route with a bicycle. Although perhaps a unicycle or a tricycle could also work. As to what kind, that's up to you. If all you've got is a full-suspension mountain bike, that'll do. If you're one of those gear heads who has 8 bikes, surely one will also do. This route has been done on every kind of bike there is, including tandem bikes, commuter bikes, and old steel fixies. If you have a gravel bike, that'll definitely work. Run whatcha brung, ain't no shame heyuh. 

After Party

Following the ride, there will be food, libations, yard games and music back at Headwaters. Capping the night off with a campfire and s'mores for those who choose to spend the night!  

Music this year by the hyper local (down the road!!) musical wonder: Keith Briggs! 

Camping 

Free car, tent, van, bus camping to anyone who wants it Saturday and Sunday night. Saturday night you'll mostly be on your own as we will be setting up for the event. Sunday night we'll be having a campfire with smore's. There will be porto-potties and a water jug, otherwise bring everything you need! 

Safety

Unfortunately, riding a bicycle, particularly on roads also traveled by cars, can be a dangerous activity. We take safety at this event super seriously and we hope you will too. Our safety measure include: 

  • An emergency plan to be shared with all riders prior to ride day so they know what to do in the event of an emergency on the course
  • Our med team will be riding sweep
  • Check-in and check-out to ensure everyone makes it off the course safely
  • First aid kit available at all aid stations and at basecamp 

Volunteers 

Aren't much of a biker, but still want to be a part of the fun? Give us a hand by parking cars, handing out snacks, or retrieving directional arrows after the ride. Select “Volunteer” on the registration page and get a free meal ticket in return! 

 

 

Community Partners 

.                    .                     .                                             

 

 

Why This Place Matters

The Crooked River is more than just a beautiful backdrop — it’s the beating heart of the Sebago Lake watershed. Its cold, clean waters are critical spawning grounds for landlocked Sebago salmon (Salmo salar sebago), a unique strain of salmon found only in the Sebago watershed. The river also helps supply drinking water to nearly 1 in 6 Mainers, making its health vital to communities far beyond its banks.

That’s why local partners like Mahoosuc Land Trust, Greater Lovell Land Trust, and Sebago Clean Waters are working hard to protect the Crooked River headwaters — keeping forests intact, water clean, and this incredible place thriving for generations to come.

In 2024, local paddlers and storytellers Andy Gagne and Jenny O'Connell and friends called attention to the river’s importance by paddling from its headwaters all the way to Casco Bay. Checkout their award-winning documentary, Follow the Water, made in partnership with Maine Mountain Media. 

Financial Transparency

The Crooked River Rambler is put on by Headwaters Maine, LLC; a recreation basecamp business owned by husband and wife Jordan Rowell and Haley Cushing. The goal for the event is first and foremost to have a great time with friends and explore this beautiful area we call home! We keep registration costs to the bare minimum, covering food, music, aid station supplies, stickers, and other random incidentals. We send $100-200 to each community partner after the event. Sometimes we're able to keep a couple hundred bucks to pay us for our time organizing, but that's really just a bonus.

What This Ride Is

It’s a chance to:

  • Get to know your Northtowne team
  • If this is your first group ride, welcome and experience the fun!

 

Ride Details

  • All bike types welcome: e-bikes, trikes, recumbents, traditional bikes
  • Route:
  • Registration closes October 7
