Welcome to the 9th edition of the Barry-Roubaix Fall Fondo Benefit Ride!

 

The Barry-Roubaix invites you to join us on October 11th, 2026 for the 9th edition of the Fall Fondo presented by Fox Subaru. Once again, this Fall ride is being organized to raise funding for the Barry County Animal Shelter & The Barry County Imagination Library. 
The ride will start in one mass group at Noon and will be led by police escort out of the City of Hastings, Fish Hatchery Park and on to the Barry-Roubaix course. Once on the course, you're welcome to ride the 18, 36 or 62 mile routes and ride at whatever pace you'd like. The courses will not be heavily marked (like on race day) with only the permanent signs at turns. We encourage you to download GPX routes or print off maps or cue sheets from our maps and files page. Each distance will have a group sweeper, but you should come prepared to self-support your ride.

Details:

  •  Ride Date: Sunday October 11th, 2026
  • Ride Time: 62 mile riders go off at 11am followed by 18/36 mile at noon
  • Ride Start Location: Fish Hatchery Park 1011 W Green St Hastings, MI 49058
  • Rider check in 9:00am - Noon EST (Barry-Roubaix tents)
  • $35 entry fee (Day of registration $55)
  • Included with your ride registration:
    • Fall Fondo handlebar plate
    • Sponsor samples
    • Pre-ride 9:30 - 11:30 am - apples, donuts and hot coffee
    • Ride hydration at start; water and Skratch
    • Post ride 1:30 - 4 pm - Soup or chili, snacks and beverages
    • Swag raffle at 3:30 pm
    • A large tent and seating to relax, socialize and snack
  • The Barry County Animal Shelter & The Barry County Imagination Library
       will be the beneficiary organizations for the 2026 event
  • Teams and individuals are welcome to set up tents on the Fish Hatchery lawn
  • There are restrooms in the park and we will have additional porta-johns setup
  • Expect beautiful Fall colors along the ride routes which are 80% dirt roads
  • Ideal bikes; Gravel, Mountain or Fatbike

No refunds, transfers or deferrals as this is a fundraiser for local organizations.

Welcome to the 30th season of the NCCX series.  We are excited to have you racing. This season's race schedule has a few changes.  If you have questions at the races, please look for our friendly NCCX Ambassadors located at registration and around the race course. From beginner to experienced racers, there are opportunities for all to participate and compete. 

Registration- All registrations will be online. There is a discount for pre-registration, and we encourage everyone to choose this option.  Early registration discount ends on Thursday night for all Saturday races, and Friday night for all Sunday races. Race day registration is available and will be online via your mobile device. 

Race Numbers- If you did not participate in the first race of the season, you must purchase a 2026 race number; the race number fee is included in registration. If you have a 2026 race number, a discount will be applied to your entry fee. Please save your number and adhere your timing chips carefully to the top of your helmet. Race numbers are made of fabric and will be used throughout the season. If you lose or forget your race number, there is a $5 replacement fee.

Refunds of registration- There will be no registration refunds. 

Volunteer- Volunteers are needed for select race weekends to help set up and tear down. A few minutes to help out at the end of the day goes a long way! View the needs and sign up here.

E-BIKE MEN AND WOMEN CATEGORIES – THIS IS WILL BE A SPORT CLASS CATEGORY AND WILL FOLLOW SPORT CLASS COURSES/DISTANCES
E-BIKE REGULATIONS (THIS IS A WORK IN PROGRESS....LEARNING AS WE GO....)
As we continue to provide e-bike racing in the Month of Mud series we want it to be a safe but welcoming racing environment for all mountain bike enthusiasts and racers. In order to do so we believe the following standards are fair for our local grassroots series.
• E- Bikes that are USAC UCI or GNCC certified are legal.
• E-Bikes must pedal assist with a max speed of 20mph.
• Programmable E-Bikes must be set and locked to 750 watts and 20 MPH. • Throttle mechanisms are prohibited. • Boost buttons must be removed or disabled. • No aftermarket modifications will be allowed.
• E-Bikes must be inspected 30 minutes before the race start. • E-Bikes MUST be in the off position at the starting line and powered up at the official's instructions. • Settings must be verified immediately after finishing. • Any E-Bike that is found to be illegal, rider will forfeit all prizes and points and will be suspended for remaining races. All categories. • Officials carry the right to test any E-Bike in question. Month of mud is not liable for any damage that may occur during testing. If you withhold your E-Bike to this test, you will be disqualified from the race.
• Passing etiquette must be followed. Unsportsmanlike behavior, foul riding, use of profanity, or flagrant discourtesy directed at participants, spectators, or officials will result in disqualification.
• Analog bikes have the right of way, you must yield to a racer in a different class to pass you when appropriate and safe to do so.
• No battery swapping during the race
 
OTHER NOTES:
· Helmets are required for all races.
· Please arrive early to check in. Check-in closes 30 minutes prior to start times.

EventAddress: 99 W Kidds Mill Rd, Greenville, PA 15164
EventNotes:
Join us for an all-day, no-pressure ride on the Shenango River Trail / Towpath. One of PA's most overlooked technical corridors. Not a race, no timing, two-way rider traffic the whole day. Just a good trail and a reason to spend the day on it.

When:
October 11th (10/11, binary, we see you nerds)

Where:
99 W Kidds Mill Rd, Greenville, PA 15164

Map:
https://caltopo.com/m/9TBC19S

Two out-and-back routes, same trailhead.
Short Trip: Kidds Mill to New Hamburg back to Kidds Mill (~8.5-9 mi)
Long Haul: Kidds Mill to Big Bend to Kidds Mill (~17.5 mi)

Natural-surface trail, a few stream crossings, mostly flat with some sudden technical ups and downs. Real terrain, not a paved cruise or flow trail. There's lots of place where you might even need to hike a bike. At least I do. The corridor also sees regular use from local equestrian groups and trail runners.

The trail follows the Shenango River. Pennsylvania's 2021 River of the Year, and hosts numerous kayak races of its own along much of the corridor. Probably going to see some herons, eagles, kingfishers. Nature!

Riders of all skill levels welcome! This is as much about getting people out on the Shenango Trail.

EventName: Falkorburg Cross -- Event #3 of the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series
EventNotes:
Event Name: Falkorburg Cross, Event #3 in the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series

Hosted by Baltimore Bicycle Works Racing

When: Sunday October 11th, 2026

Venue: Berg Farm, STM Coaching, Stevenson, MD 

Venue Address: Please follow these coordinates to the parking area, 39°24'47.0"N 76°42'54.5"W, Stevenson, MD 21153.  

Parking & Gear Drop-off: There is limited parking on site at the venue (yellow in the image below), carpooling is encouraged. There will be a gear drop so bikes, gear, and people can be dropped off as close to the action as possible. Navigation to race and the gear drop is best using the following coordinates:  39°24'47.0"N 76°42'54.5"W  Entrance for the drop-off and parking is off of Stevenson Rd. Between Valley Acres Dr. and Old Valley Rd. just past the Stevenson Village Shopping Center. The overflow parking will be at the Stevenson Village Shopping Center itself; however we've never needed to use it. Parking opens at 6:30am.  Draft course map.

 

Gender Equality & Transgender Policy: Classes designated “Masters” are open to Men and Women. Minimum Racing Age and categories quoted are for Men; please see the current USAC Rulebook for minimum Racing Age and categories for Women.  The Super Series  welcomes everyone to participate in the gender category they feel is most appropriate to them, as described in USA Cycling policies: https://usacycling.org/about-us/governance/transgender-athletes-policy.

or

The Venue: The home of Falkorburg Cross, Berg Farm, is nestled in the picturesque valleys of Baltimore County. It features a historic stone barn which holds registration and will shelter anyone looking for cover. As usual we’ll have a food truck and beer garden to keep you fed and hydrated. 

 

RACE DAY FOOD: Get your taste buds ready!

We've got Globe coffee in the morning serving up delicious coffee and some breakfast, then Ryleighs Oyster House will be on site 11am-4pm, we will also have Taharka ice cream and tasty beers available from Peabody Heights.

 

*While usually open to the public, the course will be closed beginning Friday, October 9th for course prep and will re-open on race day.

**Pre-ride opens at 7:30 am on the day of the event with the first race starting at 9:00am.  Warming up on the course during races is not permitted. All USAC rules apply.

 

The Course: The course is located on the Berg Farm in Stevenson, MD. This is a dedicated cyclocross course that is available for practicing throughout most of the year. Waivers are available on-site and required for anyone interested in scouting the course outside of set-up weekend and event day. However, we will have a few tweaks up our sleeves specifically for race day. The terrain is fast and flowing with a number of technical turns and short super punchy climbs. You won’t find any Belgian walls here, but you’ll find plenty of off-camber and twisty turns. 

The flyover is back this year! All fields, adult and junior, will pass over (and under) the flyover. We've added rungs along the left side of both the climb and descent to provide optional additional traction to anyone walking the feature. To walk, run, or ride is a common decision a rider makes when navigating any cyclocross course feature. Please remember to ride within your abilities, stay safe, and keep the rubber side down. 

Rest assured, the balance between power and technical will make this course a leveled playing field.  

 

Spectating:  The venue features easy access to all course locations.  Want to see your favorite rider zoom around the course and navigate the technical turns? No problem! You can enjoy a tasty beverage by team sponsor Peabody Heights Brewer, and watch the ‘cross action’ unfold from one central location or investigate the many prime areas throughout the course for great spectating and friendly heckling. Bring your chair and your ID, and stay around to watch the elite field fly through the course. Bringing the kids? We’ll have 10a.m. and 12p.m. Little Belgians races for the wee little ones age 9 and under. Top it off with food and coffee from local vendors. 

 

Lil Belgians Kids' Races: FREE races for kids ages 9 and under. Helmets are required, a guardian must be present and sign a release (available at the registration tent). NO racing license required. Space is limited to 50 kids, and for everyone's convenience, please pre-register online at https://www.bikereg.com/falkorburg2024 to guarantee your spot.

Registration, Entry Fees, & Licensing:  all registration and payment for this event, including race day registration, will be conducted through BikeReg.  Addtional entries are offered at $20 ($25 on race day) when purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  If the entries are purchased separately during the pre-registration period, contact us for a partial refund; on event day a coupon code will be made available at the day-of registration table to achieve the same discounted price.  Entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $30 for Junior Men for race day registration (all Junior Women race free this year), to reflect the day-of surcharge.  There will be no in-person sales at the event -- register online, either at home before coming out or on your phone at the event.  You MUST present your racing license (if you have one) or 1-Day receipt in order to be issued a bib, and you should also be prepared to show your confirmation email.  In order to expedite your entry, make sure you have completed the online waiver before approaching the day-of registration table.

This page will re-open for day-of registration by 6 AM;  check-in will open by 7 AM.  Check-in and registration for all races will close 15 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race.  There will be no exceptions made to this rule -- plan to show up timely for the race you want to enter.

Thanks to our sponsors, U19 Women may race in any class they qualify for by Cyclocross category, but remain eligible for free entry (use code Watch_Out_Boys), if registering for and girls category, there will be no fee (except Mabra charge).  For race day entry, the day-of surcharge will be applied as appropriate.  Any current National Cyclocross Champions shall be granted free entry, but must wear their national jersey in the class in which it was won.

Also thanks to sponsor generosity, BBWR is able offer complimentary entry to the first 10 BIPOC riders who register.  Please use the ‘Contact Us’ link at the bottom of this page to request the coupon code.

 

A USA Cycling racing license is required for entry.  Riders who do not provide a USAC Annual racing license # at registration will be assessed an additional $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This license is valid for entry only in fields that are open to Novice Men, Women, or Non-Binary riders.  For all other fields, you must present proof of an active USAC racing license (or a printed Authorization to Ride) showing your Cyclocross category and Racing Age.

Staging & Call Ups: Cat 5 Men's and Cat 4/5 Women’s races are staged based on pre-registration order. The rest of the races are staged according to Super Series standing for the top 8 positions and then based on CrossResults.com rankings for the remainder of pre-registered riders. Race categories and staging information is available https://www.superseriescx.com/about-1. The "Race Day Schedule" table below also provides staging information. 

 

Points: Points are awarded for Series ranking to the following Super Series categories – Men Cat 1,2,3; Women Cat 1,2,3; Men Cat 3, Men Cat 4; Masters 40+ Cat 1,2,3; Masters 50+ Cat 1,2,3,4; Masters 40+/50+ Cat 3, 4, 5; Singlespeed Men, Singlespeed Women; all U19.; Men Cat 5 and Women Cat 4/5 beginner races are not ranked. Professional chip time results by Insight Timing Services. See the Super Series Website for full details about rules and regulations for series points; https://www.superseriescx.com.

Prizes:

.Mens and Womens Cats 1/2/3 will be awarded prize money!  $300 5 Deep

. All other Adults will receive prizes at the promoter’s discretion; typically 5 deep for Falkorburg Cross.

. Juniors will receive medals three places deep.

. Lil’ Belgians races will have medals and snacks for all.

. Single Speed - The legendary traveling Cat Trophies will be back again for the Men’s and Women’s SSCX races this year. Who will claim the coveted trophy this year and win the rights to host the trophy in their home until next year? Plus podium prizes, 5 deep. 

Team tents: Premium tent spots are available for reservation through BikeReg and include one reserved parking spot near the team tent area (so, yeah…you’re really just paying for primo parking). No reservation? No problem. There’s plenty of room for all at Falkorburg Cross. You can use the drop-off loop for your gear and add your tent to the party. Important: For the 2026 Season USAC is requiring teams setting up a tent in a designated team area (pre-paid tent spaces for Falkorburg Cross), to arrive with proof of USAC Safe Sport Certification Safe Sport Training | USA Cycling. This applies to one individual representative for the team who must be present to gain access to the tent row. This requirement does not apply to all of the first-come, first-serve, unreserved team tents that are set up outside of the premium tent spots. 

 

 

 

Contacts:

FalkorburgCX@gmail.com 

Additional info at: facebook.com/falkorburgcx/ 

and https://baltimorebicycleworksracing.com/falkorburg-cx

Categories.CategoryName: MTB 40 mile trail CHILL (no race i'm just trying to survive!)

EventNotes:
All Proceeds Benefit the East Haddam Land Trust 

The Nutmeg 40 is a unique 40-mile adventure loop that utilizes the most interesting and challenging public preserves in East Haddam, Salem, and Lyme, Connecticut. The most iconic portion of this loop is the The Goodwin Trail. This is a unique, 13.5 mile linear trail that winds its way through preserved lands owned by local land trusts, municipalities, the Yale School of Forestry, and Nehantic State Park.  

Ride begins and ends at Yankee Cider, 23 Petticoat Lane, East Haddam, 06423.  Parking, restrooms, and rider meetings at Yankee Cider, then we will complete a challenging and scenic 40 mile loop traversing as-much-trail as possible . You will be very happy to see Yankee Cider upon the completion of the loop… we promise!  

Everybody who registers before Sept 20, will receive a free, Ronnie Romance designed Nutmeg 40, 2026 t-shirt. We will ask you for your shirt size in the custom question section of the registration.

The course is unmarked, so a navigation device will be required

GPX route will be emailed to registrants the Thursday before the event.

A mountain bike with sturdy tires and low gearing is recommended

Sorry no Ebikes 

Stocked rest stops every 10 miles on the course, which includes water.

In addition to riding off-road on the Goodwin Trail, cyclists will be riding through The Lena Preserve, The Jewett Preserve, The Johnstone Preserve, and many others that will all blend together in a mind bender of a day out on the bike.

The Goodwin Trail, and the other single tracks you will encounter (while 99 percent rideable) are a technical test of your off-roading skills on a bicycle – this is the longest, most remote mountain bike event in the state, and entrants should be prepared for a physical test/challenge to remember.  This will be a timed race for those who choose to race, and an all day trail adventure for those who want to take it at their own pace.    

This will be a challenging event for many of us. Please give careful consideration before registering. 

We will create rest/refreshment stops along the way. All the snacks will be homemade - probably lots of banana bread. We will have sandwiches, fruit, and goodies at about the ½ way point and hearty vegetarian chili and cornbread at the end at Yankee Cider. A variety of locally made, cold, hard and soft cider will be available at the cash bar upon your return.  You will be well fed this day. Please specify any severe or life-threatening food allergies when you register.  Lastly, we cannot guarantee an allergen-free environment due to shared kitchen facilities.

Pease carry your own water, snacks, and other needed accessories as well.  There are places where a water filter might come in handy.  

Cell service is very inconsistent on the trail. We strongly recommend participating with a buddy or two. We will provide a sweeper who could provide hands-off assistance. Please note that it could take skilled medical/mechanical staff up to two hours to reach you on the trail. 

We will host the event in rain. We will cancel if there are strong storms. Please check the EHLT website and Facebook pages for last minute updates.

Your registration donation will help East Haddam Land Trust preserve and steward land in perpetuity for all of us to enjoy, and earn you a 1-year membership to EHLT. Your membership entitles you to advanced notice to our hikes, paddles, and other fun events as well as allowing you to participate in members-only experiences. We are grateful for your help. 

Please note that if this event is cancelled for any reason, we will continue to accept your donation to EHLT and not issue refunds. Thank you for understanding this.

Please sign the online waiver form before you arrive.

Please arrive to Yankee Cider, 23 Petticoat Lane, East Haddam, CT 06423 from 7:30am- 8:15am. We will host a short meeting for all cyclists at 8:15am then those who are racing will leave followed by the recreational cyclists. 

Please learn about the Eightmile River Watershed, which hosts the Goodwin Trail, and find trail maps here:

https://www.eightmileriver.org/outdoor-recreation/
PresentedBy: East Haddam Land Trust and Ron's Bikes

Get Ready for Revenant Cross Weekend!
Presented by ATC Racing | DNA Cycling

We're kicking off the Austin cyclocross season with Revenant Cross at Richard Moya Park in Austin, TX, part of the TXCX series so don’t miss it. With CX Nationals in Fayetteville, AR Dec 9–13, 2026, race with us now to earn USA Cycling points and improve your starting position there.

Expect a course that’s as fun as it is fierce – packed with off-camber turns, punchy climbs, and fast, flowy sections that'll keep your heart racing and your tires turning.

Spectators, this one's for you too! This course is super viewer-friendly, so bring your cowbells, cheers, and your best heckles – racers love it.

New to cyclocross? No worries – we’ve got a race category for everyone, from first-timers to seasoned CX pros. Come race, cheer, hang out, and be part of the scene.

Cyclocross is the perfect way to sharpen your bike skills, test your grit, and most importantly – have an absolute blast doing it.

Sign up now, rally your riding buddies, and get ready for a weekend of mud, sweat, and cheers!

Revenant Cross Weekend is calling – will you answer?

Follow us on Social Media to stay up to date on Revenant Cross!

Instagram:  atc_racing_atx

TikTok: atc_racing_atx

Race rules:

  1. Don’t be a jerk.
  2. Abide by all USAC cyclocross rules.
  3. The promoter’s ruling is final.
  4. Gravel and mountain bikes without bar ends are allowed. No maximum tire widths enforced. 
  5. Please inform the finish line judges if you withdraw from the race. 
  6. Awards will be awarded 3 deep in competitive categories. Depending on field size, promoter may expand to 5 deep.
  7. Please patronize our sponsors.
  8. You must check in with the registration staff to be counted in the results.

 

Entry Fees

Entry fee is $40 for your first race and includes any additional races on the same day (ex. Novice riders may also enter the 3/4/Novice field on the same day at no additional cost).  Note: You must register for these at the same time to take advantage of this discount.

On-site registration will be available this year. Entries after midnight on Thursday 10/29 will incur a $10 late fee and may not be included in call-ups. Registration closes 30 minutes before each race wave, so we highly encourage you to sign up as soon as you can. Call-ups will be by crossresults.com.

 

Racing Licenses

All competitive categories require a USA Cycling license to participate. If you do not have a current USAC annual license you can purchase one at memberships.usacycling.org. Licenses are good for a period of one year and cover road, mountain, gravel, track, and cyclocross racing. If you get your license now, you'll be prepared for the rest of the TXCX series.

 

Parking and Directions

Ample parking is available in the lots at Richard Moya Park for no additional fee. Please respect park speed limits and be cognizant of bicycles and pedestrians inside the park. 

 

Weather

The event is rain or shine. Delays or cancellations may be issued at the discretion of the promoter or race officials in the event of severe weather.

 

Mechanical Support

Austin Tri Cyclist will be on-hand with neutral mechanical support all weekend. Conveniently located near the pit in case you need any mid-race fixes.

BIRDEYE ULTRA

UNSUPPORTED. UNREASONABLE. UNFORGETTABLE.

 

 

THE CHALLENGE

Two routes. One starting line. Birdeye.

BIRDEYE 500

Ride the entire Crowley’s Ridge Gravel Trail—twice.

An enormous self-supported journey through the Arkansas Delta, connecting rural communities, state parks, gravel roads, and the full length of Crowley’s Ridge.

NIGHT OWL 200

Ride from Birdeye to Helena and back.

A long beautiful ride through the Delta for those looking to push themselves without committing to the full 500.

 

THE RULES ARE SIMPLE.

Ride the route.

That's it.

This is a free, self-timed, unsupported adventure.

We provide the route, a suggested start time, and a finish line in Birdeye.

You provide the legs, the logistics, the navigation, the snacks, and whatever it takes to get yourself home.

Your bike. Your pace. Your adventure.

THE REWARD

There is no giant trophy.

No cash prize.

No podium.

The reward is finishing something that looked a little ridiculous when you signed up.

It's the satisfaction of covering the miles, solving the problems, pushing through the hard parts, and rolling back into Birdeye under your own power.  

And, of course, making it back in time for dinner.

Finish the route and add your name to the short list of Birdeye Ultra finishers.

FIND OUT WHAT YOU'RE MADE OF.

Ride with friends.
Push the pace.
Race somebody who wants to race.
Or disappear down the road and make it a solo mission.

Use it as training for your next big one, a bikepacking adventure with your buds, or simply as an excuse to do something completely unreasonable.

However you choose to ride it, we're here to stoke the fire.

THE ROUTES

BIRDEYE 500 Route

NIGHT OWL 200 Route

Looking for beta?
Explore the Crowley’s Ridge Gravel Trail route collection.

Important: These are unofficial routes. Route conditions can change. You are responsible for your own navigation, safety, equipment, food, water, and logistics. Trackleaders registration is required: https://form.jotform.com/trackleaders/birdeye26

There is NO rolling SAG.

If you need a bailout, call your bestie.

THE CLOCK IS YOURS.

Start whenever you want.

Leave Birdeye on any date and at any time that works for your adventure.

The only requirement:

Be back in Birdeye by dinner on Saturday, November 7.

That's your finish line.

THE SELFIE BONUS

Hit the Arkansas State Parks along the route?

Prove it.

Post your State Park selfies, tag Studio Drift, and you'll be entered to win prizes.

Ride the miles. Collect the parks. Tell the story.

MORE THAN A RIDE

Birdeye Ultra is part of studioDRIFT's mission to build a stronger Arkansas Delta through outdoor recreation and community.

Your participation helps studioDRIFT continue investing in trails, outdoor recreation, cultural programming, and the rural communities that make the Delta special.

EventName: JM Collingwood Barn Rat Filthy 50 Gravel
EventNotes:
Join us at the historic JM Collingwood Barn, west of Pretty Prairie, Kansas in the beautiful Ninnescah River Valley! The largest barn in Kansas, built in 1913, is a hidden gem and you'll be in awe of its architectural craftsmanship! 

 

The routes will head south from the barn into Kingman County this year, exploring the roller hills, bluffs, and open grasslands between Murdock and Kingman.

The roads in our area of Kansas range from fast hard pack to light sand over hard pack with some stretches of deeper sand that change in firmness with rainfall amounts. We do our best to limit the amount of deep sand, but it is all part of the challenge in the Ninnescah River Valley.

REGISTRATION FEE INCLUDES YOUR CHOICE OF A LONG-SLEEVED OR SHORT-SLEEVED T-SHIRT, A HOLOGRAPHIC STICKER,  A HOMEMADE POST-RIDE SOUP AND CINNAMON ROLL MEAL (MEAT AND VEGETARIAN OPTIONS), AND AN OPTIONAL CRAFT BEER FROM SANDHILLS BREWING. REGISTER BY OCTOBER 14TH TO GUARANTEE A T-SHIRT BY EVENT DAY.

    

YOU MAY BUY ADDITIONAL MERCHANDISE ITEMS IF YOU WISH…Extra t-shirts from this year and previous years' events, stickers, and meal vouchers for supporters that attend with you. 

The top 3 riders of each race will receive a custom award created by talented, local artists. First place will again this year be a one-of-a-kind metalwork barn rat award. Photos of the awards will be posted on social media closer to the event.

After your ride, relax in the spacious barn loft with a traditional Midwest soup and cinnamon roll meal. Brenda's Taco Soup or The Blew Heeler Special Tomato Soup by The Blew Heeler and cinnamon rolls from the Cozy Coop, both of Pretty Prairie. 

Sandhills Brewing of Hutchinson will be joining us with their craft beer for those that wish to partake.

Enjoy the music of John Depew of Arlington post-ride in the loft.

We are raising money for our local non-profit, the Pretty Prairie Community Food Pantry, 501(c)(3), as they are in need of a new backup generator to prevent food loss in case of a power outage. Meal proceeds of each registration go to the Food Pantry and you may also donate to their cause in the merchandise section. We thank you so very much in advance for your generosity.

If you live a good distance from here and wish to arrive the night before, as to not have to drive too far the morning of the ride, there are options for lodging close by! We include a list of local places to stay in the confirmation email when you register, but you can contact us for that list, as well.

Go Nuts Regionals (GNR) eMTB Rules as follows:  1) Maximum 750watts - assistance up to 20 miles per hour - Pedaling assistance only. No hand or foot throttle allowed. Automatic disqualification. Bicycles must remain locked, i.e., no modification of wheel sensor from factory circumference or any other modification to manipulate the factory set speed of the bike.?2) Throttle mechanisms are prohibited.?3) Studded tires are prohibited.?4) It is forbidden to change e-bike during the event even if the rider finishes the event with the same race plate.?5) It is forbidden to recharge the e-bike or battery in the technical zone during the GNR event.?6) Technical assistance consists of the replacement or repairs of any part of the e-bike at the exception of the frame, wheels or battery.?7) Riders age categories are 18 and under, 19-39, 40-49 and 50 plus for Classes; Amateurs, Experts and Open Pro.  8) Riders can only use the battery in place on their bike and cannot carry or switch out an additional battery during the competition.?9) Race course length will be 4.5 - 7 miles depending on difficulty. Steeper climbs and more technical than normal XC will be tested on some courses. Each category will start an hour apart and should be completed within their hour.?10) Races will be conducted regardless of weather conditions.  In the event of rain or other unfavorable conditions, it may be necessary to alter the order of the event schedule, including but not limited to, adjusting the length of the race or delaying or stopping the program completely.  Should a delay occur, every effort will be made to resume the schedule in a timely fashion if conditions significantly improve.?11) No headphones, earphones or sound devices permitted. Horns and bells are permitted.?12) Riders are required to wear the appropriate helmet. Other protective gear is optional; gloves, goggles, elbow/knee guards, etc.?13) Shirt, shoes, and pants/shorts required. Clipless or flat pedals are both permitted.?15) An E-Mountain Bike is a bike operated with two energy sources, human pedal power and an electric engine, which only provides assistance when the rider is pedaling.?16) The course will the taped and marked. Any rider cutting the course will be disqualified.?17) Any behavior deemed in appropriate or unsportsmanlike like conduct will not be tolerated. Verbal or physical infractions will result in a disqualification.

Severe weather policy- Unless otherwise posted, race will be held. Safety of all racers is our main priority. If there is a delay or cancellation due to weather conditions, racers are responsible for checking information posted by director.?The information will be posted on the homepage of website, social network avenues, and via email up to 72 hours prior to the race.

Transfer/Refund Policy-There will be no registration refunds once registration is processed. We will allow transfers to upcoming races. All transfers must be requested 10 days prior and is only allowed for races that were rescheduled. Transfers will not be allowed 10 days before race or after race.

The Ponderosa Gravel Race is back and will be held at the Elk City Hall. Come race with us on Halloween!! Let's have some fun with some costumes. Check in will start at 6:30am inside the hall. Other than the aid stations on course, this is a self supported race. There will be an emergency contact # on the back of your race plate. We'll be manually timing this race so be patient. Podium's for top 3 in each category will follow shortly after all 3 have finished. 

Special thanks to The Ponderosa Bar, MGrill's and Kinney MFG, Goodlife Nutrition, Foothill Products for all their support.

FIRST EDITION OF THE DOÑA ANA MOUNTAIN RACE 2026

This MTB Race takes place in the South DA Mountains in Las Cruces, New Mexico and is scheduled for October 31st (8:00 AM start). Packet pick-up and in-person registration is at FYZICAL (Las Cruces NM) on Friday, October 30th from 2:00-6:00.

Course options include a "Real" beginner's course of 6 miles (open to young riders) and a “Novice” course of 12 miles.

The Chainsmoker Mountain Bike Race returns for its 5th year, bringing riders back to one of Southern Nevada's most challenging and rewarding endurance events. Whether you're new to mountain biking or a seasoned racer looking to test your limits, there's a distance for you.

Choose from the Little Smoker (11 miles), the original Chainsmoker (22 miles), or take on the ultimate challenge with the 44-mile ultra-distance event. Riders will experience a mix of fast-flowing trails, technical terrain, challenging climbs, and rewarding descents, all set against the stunning backdrop of the Nevada desert.

The Chainsmoker is designed to be fun, competitive, and welcoming to riders of all skill levels. From first-time racers to experienced endurance athletes, everyone is encouraged to come out, challenge themselves, and enjoy a great day on the trails.

The event will begin at 8:00 AM in the Blue Diamond public park. Registered participants will receive detailed rider information prior to race day, including course details, parking instructions, packet pickup information, and event logistics.

Join us as we celebrate Year 5 of the Chainsmoker and see if you have what it takes to earn your finish.

The Team at NYC Velo

Search and State All Road Apparel

Chris McNally Drawing Studio

We're following up the success of the first 2 editions of the Fire Tower Brevet (thanks to all of you who took part!) with a new route & 5 new towers!  The new route spends little time in our beloved Hudson Valley, opting for adventures westward.  This new uncharted terrain (by Fire Tower Brevet standards) includes immersion in the New Jersey Highlands, the Delaware Valley, and the Pocono Mountains of Pennsylvania.  The new route for FT3 explores notable areas of Northern NJ & Eastern PA: Hackensack & Patterson NJ, High Mountain Park, Jungle Habitat, High Point State Park, Stairway Wild Area, Hickory Run Forest, Hell Mountain, and, notably, Staten Island.  While there are some lengthy sections of flat terrain, the 5 Fire Tower ascents include gradients, often unpaved, that can exceed 20% (all 5 tower ascents this year are rideable, apologies again for the gut punch that was Mt Beacon).  Though it may be argued that this ride isn't for everyone we've made accommodations so that those of you uninterested in a death march in the mountains can still enjoy a great adventure:

  • The goal of the Fire Tower Brevet is to push the limits a bit of Brevet-style riding and to explore parts of the Mid-Atlantic & Hudson Valley regions that may be off the radar of NYC cyclists.  Scroll down for details of the ride & prizes, and links to the route. The ride is Brevet-style, starting and ending at NYC Velo - East Village (66 2nd Avenue)
  • The 5 Controles (checkpoints) on the route are 5 historical Fire Towers throughout Northern NJ & the Pocono Mountains of Pennsylvania, chosen for their location and bike accessibility, these include:
    • Ramapo Station Fire Tower (Heart hole punch)
    • Buckhorn Ridge Fire Tower (Rectangle hole punch)
    • High Knob Fire Tower (Star hole punch)
    • Pohopoco Fire Tower (Diamond hole punch)
    • Mauch Chunk (Bear Mountain) Fire Tower (Circle hole punch)
  • The "Suggested Route" is approximately 330 miles. Riders are not required to follow the route, only to visit the 5 Controles
  • Riders who plan to participate are required to register here on BikeReg and will be issued a Brevet card (designed by the artist Chris McNally)
  • At each Controle there will be a uniquely-shaped hole punch used to punch the corresponding Fire Tower on the Brevet card
  • Riders will also produce digital proof of successful Controle check-in/route completion (via a GPS/Strava file and/or Instagram/social media photos of themselves at the Controle) to qualify for the tiered Rewards
  • The official ride start is 5:00am Saturday July 11 2026 at NYC Velo East Village though riders may complete their own adventure at anytime between July 11 and 11:59pm October 31 2026
  • This is an unsupported ride – riders are responsible for their own navigation, hydration, nutrition, equipment, and safety - the use of e-bikes, cars, trains, etc are prohibited for Tier 1 & Tier 2 consideration
  • Riders should take appropriate caution riding on open roads, use appropriate lighting for low light or night time riding conditions, and use appropriate safety gear at all times (including helmets, reflective apparel, etc)

 

The Suggested Route:

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/55755950
 


The Tiers of Participation:

  1. Tier 1 Participation: Riders must start and end at NYC Velo East Village and complete all 5 Controles within 48 hours.  Riders may follow any route but may use only 1 human-powered bicycle (i.e. no e-bikes, trains, or Ubers).  Riders who complete the course (starting & ending at NYC Velo East Village) and collect punches at the 5 Controles in any 48-hour period from opening day (July 11) through October 31 2026 will present documentation to Andrew at NYC Velo East Village or by emailing info@nycvelo.com.
  2. Tier 2 Participation: riders complete the course in 1 continuous ride but take longer than 48 hours but less than 120 hours -- for example if they want to expand the route to take 4 or 5 days and visit other locations in the Catskills, or they simply want to stretch the ride across more days (starting & ending at NYC Velo East Village).  Tier 2 Participation will be open through October 31 2026.
  3. Tier 3 Participation: riders complete all 5 Controles on separate visits over any length of time (weeks or months), but always by bike.  Controles may be completed over separate outings and in any order.  Tier 3 Participation will be open through October 31 2026.  

Rewards:

  1. For successful Tier 1 completion: Coleman Camp of Type 3 in Brooklyn has come on board to make custom Musette Bags, available for the first 20 riders to successfully complete the Tier 1 challenge.  Tier 1 winners will also receive a custom Fire Tower Brevet enamel pin and sticker pack.
  2. For successful Tier 2 completion: NYC Velo will send out a custom Fire Tower Brevet enamel pin, sticker pack, & Search and State cycling cap (limited to the first 50 riders)
  3. For successful Tier 3 completion: NYC Velo will send out a Fire Tower Brevet sticker pack (Tier 3 is unlimited)

Additional Ride Notes:

 
Though it's assumed that all who have signed up for this adventure are seasoned and thoughtful riders, riders are implored to make safely their highest consideration when attempting the Third Fire Tower Brevet:
  • Always have appropriate lighting on you and your bike during low or no-light situations
  • Pay close attention to your hydration and nutrition plan & stay hydrated
  • Please be aware of the dangers of over heating/heat exhaustion -- trust that this ride isn't worth it
As of 7/9/26 the hole punches have been Please see below for some course notes from my recon(s) of the route:
  • The hole punch has been attached to the Southwest leg of the Ramapo Station Fire Tower
  • The hole punch has been attached to the Northeast leg of the Buckhorn Ridge Fire Tower

NOTE that as of Thursday 7/9 all hole punches were attached to their respective towers.  It is possible that this may change as time goes on and other punches disappear - if that happens just document your visit to the tower (i.e. Ramapo Station, etc) with a selfie - there is a backup set of punches in the shop and you can get your card punched after the fact, just record the time with a photo (and send it to info@nycvelo.com) for credit of the Controle.
  • Be sure to tag @nycvelo and #firetowerbrevet & #FT3 on your social media posts -- thanks!
  • Be prepared with insect repellent during the ride -- you'll be swarmed by biting insects (flies, mosquitos, etc) on some sections of the route, especially on the climbs where you can't outrun them

Extra Credit:
 
Maybe it's because we've been working on this ride for so long, but we have a list of some additional can't miss things close to the "suggested" Fire Tower Brevet route.  Any registered rider who accomplishes any of the items below during their attempt at the Brevet and posts a photo of it on social media (be sure to tag @nycvelo so that I see it) will get a separate Brevet patch:
  • The first “Extra Credit” is so important that it should just be considered “Credit” – visit the High Point of NJ – it's on the route!
  • Grab a coffee or bite to eat at Abraço (81 East 7th STreet in the East Village, @abraco_espresso)
  • Make a rubbing of a Geological Survey Marker at any point on or near the course
  • Add some additional climbing on the ride (but you can deviate from the route if you like) to reach a total elevation gain of 29,032 feet (a form of "Everesting" without the 24-hour time limit)
  • Spend the night camping at a lean-to along the route.
Enjoy the ride!

For the eleventh year, Yellow Chip Road is going SPOOKY! Formerly know as Ill Kanza, this is a long running grassroots gravel grinder starting and ending in Kansas, Illinois. In contrast to the recent trend of making gravel events smoother and easier, our routes remain as gnarly as ever! Expect varied surfaces including some very rough gravel and stream crossings, rolling terrain, and remote scenery. The 104 mile route in particular has some especially rough and rocky sections, though none of the routes are easy. All routes will be timed, with prizes for the top three in each category of the 3 longest routes. All entries get raffle tickets! As anyone who's ridden here before knows, these roads can be very rough and challenging so come prepared!
 
Minimum recommended tire size: 32
Suggested tire size: 45+

--- Registration ---
 
Right here!
Or register on-site for $5 extra. A portion of the proceeds will be donated to the Kansas Food Pantry.
 
--- Start Time, Location, and Parking ---
 
The 104 mile route will start at 8 AM, the others will start at 10 AM.
Start location is the park at the corner of Front St and Jefferson St in Kansas:
https://goo.gl/maps/gsWhmNRpTs72
There is some parking available at the park, but you can also park at the lot 200 feet to the south on Buena Vista St:
https://goo.gl/maps/oCh9oWZyEEn
There should also be plenty of street parking available. Make sure not to park at the bank since it is open.
 
--- Course Info ----
 
This event will be mostly self supported. Make sure to bring spare tubes, a pump or CO2, tools, and ideally chain quick links. We will have a number you can call if you really cannot continue but for the most part riders are expected to fix problems on their own.
 
There will be two supply tables with drop bag service, supply table A and supply table B. Most courses will only visit one of them. We will collect drop bags before the event that we will run out to each table. We will also have some additional food and water available to all at the tables. There will be two additional supply tables/coolers on the 104 mile course. Here is the mile marker that each table is at on each course:
22: Table B at mile 12.4
33: Table B at mile 22.9
46: Table B at mile 36.1
72: Table A at mile 41.8, table B at mile 62.4
104: Cooler at mile 39.4, table at mile 58.7, table A at mile 91.3
 
There is also a gas station in Marshall at mile 52.8 on the 104 mile course. If you are not stopping at the Gas Station you can turn left on 6th St and cut .3 miles off the course. There is also a soda machine in Grandview at mile 48.3 on the 72 mile course.
 
We will put a sign at every turn that is on a gravel road and not at a T-intersection. The course will also be marked with pavement markings (on paved roads) and flags (everywhere). The flag will always be on the *right* side of the road just *before* the intersection, ignore flags in other locations. The flag will be pink for a right turn, and blue for a left. We will also have maps and cue sheets available. If you have a GPS we strongly suggest loading the course onto it.
 
*The 104 mile course will be completely unmarked.*
 
Keep in mind this event is held on public roads! Obey the rules of the road and watch out for traffic.
 
--- Timing/Ranking Info ---
 
The timer will start at the start time. There will be a neutral start (except for the 104 mile) until the first gravel road, 1.3 miles into the ride. The finish line will be 1.4 miles before the end of the course, near the end of the last gravel road. There will be a checkered flag sign and a person timing at the finish line. This means the timed distances are 44.6 miles for the 46 mile course, 70.8 miles for the 72 mile course, and 102.1 for the 104 mile course.
 
Make sure your number is visible to the timers as you cross the line. If you're not certain if they got you, please stop and make sure.
 
--- Food ---
 
The Kansas Food Pantry is now located at the Presbyterian Church at 304 S Franklin, and the post race meal will be served there (meal must be purchased, but it's cheap).
https://maps.app.goo.gl/vD6sX9paMAogUWFYA
 
--- Bathrooms ---
 
The bathrooms in the Presbyterian Church (see above) will be open.
 
--- Prizes / Raffle ---
 
There will be awards for the top 3 finishers in the Open 104, Women's 104, Singlespeed 104, Open 72, Women's 72, Open 46, and Women's 46 fields.
 
All participants will get 3 raffle entries - 3 sets of two matching tickets. Before the start, place one ticket from each set in the cup in front of something you want to win, and hold on to the matching tickets. After the ride, a ticket will be drawn for each prize from its cup and winning tickets will be taped to the prizes, so check and see if you won anything!

Rapture in Misery: From 24 Hours of Madness to a Mountain Biking Legend

Celebrating the legacy of a race that became a rite of passage

It Started with a Wild Idea

In 2001, a loose-knit group of mountain bikers rolled into Snow Creek chasing something few could understand — and even fewer could finish. A 24-hour mountain bike race. No glory, no fame — just headlights, hills, and a lot of pain. The idea was simple: ride until you can't, then ride a little more.

That first Rapture in Misery lit a fire. And soon, it became more than just a race. It became a legend.

The First Ride – Snow Creek, 2001

There was something gritty and pure about that first year. Snow Creek, typically known for its winter ski runs, played host to a summer sufferfest. Riders took turns circling a course that felt more like an endurance gauntlet than a bike race. People rode through the night, relying on duct tape, drive, and caffeine to hold themselves together.

There were no luxuries — just tents, cold sandwiches, and the sound of freehubs clicking through the darkness. If you were there, you still tell stories about it. If you weren’t, you’ve heard them.

Landahl Park – Technical, Raw, and Wild

After two years at Snow Creek, Rapture in Misery moved to Landahl Park, one of Missouri’s most revered singletrack trail systems. And with that shift, the race found a new kind of identity: raw, technical, and beautifully brutal.

Landahl’s terrain was a whole different animal. Tight turns, sharp climbs, off-camber descents — it wasn’t just about endurance anymore. It was about skill, timing, and knowing exactly how hard you could push without breaking... your bike or yourself.

Some came because they loved Landahl’s unforgiving charm. Others came because they’d heard about this crazy race where legends were made — and sometimes broken. Either way, it was a proving ground, and it helped cement Rapture as a must-do for Midwest endurance junkies.

Crowder State Park – Community Roots Deepen

Eventually, Rapture moved again in 2009 — this time to Crowder State Park, and with that move came a new phase. If Snow Creek was the spark and Landahl the fire, Crowder was where the fire turned into a tradition.

At Crowder, the vibe shifted from wild experiment to beloved annual gathering. The course was tough — don’t let anyone tell you otherwise — but there was something about it that brought people together. The campground felt like a mini-village each year, full of familiar faces, shared meals, and the occasional beer hand-up.

It was here that Rapture’s community really bloomed. Solo riders, team riders, rookies, and veterans all came together with a shared understanding: this race was something special.

More Than a Race – What Made RIM Special

What set Rapture in Misery apart wasn’t just the course, the miles, or the midnight hallucinations — it was the people.

There was something magnetic about the event that brought out the best (and sometimes the weirdest) in everyone. You’d see solo riders grinding out lap after lap with thousand-yard stares, and then laugh at a guy in a tutu sprinting for a handoff. You’d share tools, tubes, and war stories with people you’d just met.

It was more than a race. It was a reunion for the unreasonably driven — the community of “why-not?” people. Everyone suffered, and everyone smiled through it.

The Newest Chapter

EventNotes:
Welcome to the 2026 Fall Session of Galbraith Gravity Racing!

  • Registration closes 9/17/2026 or when capacity is reached. No late additions, we need time to matricualte. Refunds will not return uniform cost and are case by case.

  • USA Cycling License Required

  • Read all the event notes on Bike Reg. The Event Notes are below the registration form, so one must scroll down to the bottom of the page to see the notes

  • Full face enduro helmet, bike (full suspension highly reccomended) in great working order, elbow, and knee pads required.

  • U8’s require parent, gaurdian, or extra coach voluneter particpation on rides since we tow the little kids up.

  • We are a race team, all volunteer, not a fee for coaching or daycare service.

  • Racers and parents are required to sign and adhere to the GGR Code of Conduct.

  • Membership Priority is given to current and aspiring racers

  • Must be able to ride a Blue Trail tech and flow at a trail speed appropriate for their age to join. If one needs to develop skills prior to joining, there are several great skills coaches available in the area.

  • Fall Session starts 28 Spetember-31 October 2025, M-Th after school until about 6:30.

  • U14+ practice on M/W - U12 and below practice T/Th (NOTE: this may change to Mondays for older kids, Tuesday for Younger and the whole team does longer rides on Thursdays to take advantage of early release)

  • Fall Session is focused on developing a spirit of teamwork, fun, and love of riding.

Important - Getting Started:

  1. Sign up for a race license at USA Cycling prior to registering, the system will ask for your USAC license number.
  2. When signing up for your USA Cycling license - add Galbraith Gravity Racing as your team affiliation.  Any issues with USA Cycling are easily fixed by emailing: membership@usacycling.org
  3. Your GGR Fall Team membership includes entry to all GGR Fall Training Sessions.  Spring members that do not sign up for training sessions are still welcome at fun stuff you see posted on slack like BBQs, Movie Nights, Etc.

GGR is hosting a spring session starting the week of 8 Sept through 16 October.  A 6 week program.  Registration includes:

  • 5 weeks of practice'
  • Early bird registration for the Spring Session.
  • Special Team Activites

The goal of the fall session is to practice key skills, build confidence, team cohesion, endurance and experience the great fall weather.  

Please note:

  • Dates are weather and safety dependent, changes can and will occur.  We reserve the right to cancel practice/races and makeup dates may not be available.
  • Specific dates for specific age groups will be posted on the team calendar and on the team SLACK message board.
  • Nothing is mandatory to attend - racers set their own schedule
  • All racers must agree to the code of conduct.
  • GGR is a race team - not a child care service or full service coaching clinic program.  Everyone is expected to contribute, be flexible, and help the team.  Fees are used to pay insurance, buy equipment, purchase coaching certifications, etc. The purpose of the Fall Season is to clean up our form and technique from the summer racing season, and focus on some skills before the snow starts falling.
  • Makeups will occur on a case by case basis on weekends.
  • The Program is 5 weeks, 2x per week, and occasional weekend activities.

Calendar (age group groups will be moved about based on the racers needs.  We will offer a M-W option for Race Age 14+ and a T-TH option for younger age groups.   We may move Wed to Thursdays to create a longer riding day taking advantage of early release.

Times are based on sunset, but basically start a little after 4:00 ish.  Some rides can happen early for smaller kids based on coach availability.  .  Groups are made up after registration

Registering through BikeReg allows us to electronically complete waivers for all our participants, connects to USA Cycling and more. Creating a BIKEREG account when signing for membership will make it easier for signing up to races/clinic etc.  NW Cup also uses BIKEREG, so create an account if you don't already have one - it will save time in the future. 

***Please note - The event title is 'Membership Drive'.  The timeframe for membership is not the term of membership.  Team insurance and membership set to cover the entire year, through Dec 31st, 2023.  

When you join - you will gain electronic access to the team calendar and team SLACK platform - access emails are not automatic, we have to put them in manually, feel free to remind us.

Refunds - we have fixed and variable costs. If you change your mind, and need a refund, funds may not be available. Once clinics start, and jerseys have been ordered no refunds for these items will be issued.  

Appreciate your being part of the team!

V/R

Dave, Matt, Sarah and Lloyd (your board members) and the rest of the GGR Family

EventNotes:
Well HEY!  Another of year of the greatest race in the Land o' MABRA (yes, we own our bias).  

Welcome to Baltimore Youth Cycling's Frosty Cross!  We are proud to once again be hosting the MABRA Age Graded Championships!

We’re glad you'll be joining us.  This year we are back at the Agricultural Center: the same great venue and awesome course (can’t wait to see what our course designer comes up with this year).   

This year we are introducing wave starts!

All riders in a wave will start on a single whistle and results that are sent to USA Cycling will be based on the wave, not on the individual categories. Podiums and prizes at the event WILL BE broken out by category. We repeat, All riders in a wave will start on a single whistle and results that are sent to USA Cycling will be based on the wave, not on the individual categories. Podiums and prizes at the event WILL BE broken out by category.

Why are we doing this? For a few reasons – first and foremost, we believe it provides a better race experience for everyone. Riders in races with multiple classes will start based on Cross Results point meaning a rider starting on a second whistle won’t have to work through the slower riders from the first whistle right after their start. For categories with fewer riders, it means a more competitive race and a chance to work on your race-craft instead of riding around the course with only a few riders. Secondly, it provides a better opportunity for riders to earn points and better their USAC ranking. USAC points will be scored based on the wave rather than the individual field. For riders in smaller fields, this means a chance to earn points where no points would have been awarded for the smaller field. For all riders, you have the chance to earn points based on a larger pool of riders (and thus USAC points).

Location:

The Center for Maryland Agriculture is located at 1114 Shawan Rd Cockeysville, MD 21030 about one mile west of I-83. It's conveniently located a few minutes away from Hunt Valley, where you will find hotels, restaurants, coffee shops, and any other services you might need.  We have ample on-site parking.

Looking forward to a great day!!!  We've put an order in for great weather (definition of this may vary by racer).

NOTES: 

This event is held under USA Cycling permit.  All USA Cycling Cyclocross rules apply.

    •    A USAC racing license is required for all races except the kids' race (racers 8 and under).  If you do not supply a valid license # at registration you will be charged an extra $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This type of license is valid for entry only in races that are open to Novice (Cat. 5) riders.

    •    Mountain bikes are allowed; however, bar ends are NOT allowed and must be removed.
    •    MABRA Cyclocross Series rules available at http://www.mabra.org/
    •    There will be a $10 day-of surcharge added to the entry fees shown above.
    •    Junior riders ONLY may enter any non-age-graded adult race they qualify for by category at the Junior price by entering coupon code FRX_2025_JRS at checkout.
    •    Payout Parity: Top five finishers in the Men’s 1/2/3 race receive the same amount in payout as the Women’s 1/2/3. 

    •    Event will be held rain or shine.
Thanks to Gross Mendelsohn for sponsoring our elite podiums!

Warmups: The course will be open for inspection and warm-up approximately 15 minutes prior to each event. Warming up on the course during an event is strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated. DQ & forfeiture of entry fee will result.

Call-Ups: Staging will be based on the most recent Cross-Results score

    1.    All pre-registered riders will be staged on the grid, by bib number.  Bib numbers will be assigned as follows, according to ranking on CrossResults.com as of the close of registration.
    2.    Remaining riders will be staged by bib number, in the order of registration.

Those classes consisting of only cat 5 men or cat 4 women are staged by order of registration. All day-of registrants will be staged behind pre-registered riders.

Transgender policy: 

Baltimore Youth Cycling welcomes everyone to participate in the gender category they feel is most appropriate to them, as described in USA Cycling policies: https://usacycling.org/about-us/governance/transgender-athletes-policy

Women may enter any men’s race for which they are eligible by age, category, and any performance requirements. They may also enter categorized races for men that are up to one category lower than their women’s category. Category 1 women may enter men’s races up to two categories lower.

Master women may compete in men’s master's races as follows:

Category 1 and 2 master women may enter men’s events for riders up to 10 years above their racing ages;
Category 3 and 4 master women may enter men’s events for riders up to 20 years above their racing ages.

Results:  Baltimore Youth Cycling’s Frosty Cross is electronically timed. The protest period is a firm 15 minutes from the announcement that results have been posted. Racers are also reminded to make sure their team name is correct in USA Cycling, BikeReg, and on the waiver at the race.

Pit: There will be one double-sided pit on the course.  Please remove your equipment immediately following your race to make room for others.

Course Description: The course utilizes the beautiful grounds of the Maryland Agricultural Center with a balance of pavement, grass, woods and dirt paths. Much of the course winds around the Farm Center and includes hills as well as flats.

Spectating: The course has great sight lines and many opportunities for spectators to get a great view of the action. A central announcer will be located in near the Start/Finish. There will be food and beer for sale at the event and it will be good. 

Tents: The $20 fee for tent space will go to the Baltimore Youth Cycling junior racing program.

Registration:  

    •    Onsite registration opens at 7:15AM and closes 30 minutes before each race. 
    •    Second races are discounted to $15; the discount code is applied automagically if both entries are purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  For a second race purchased separately prior to event day, use the ‘Contact Event’ link  to request a partial refund; on event day, a coupon code will be provided at the day-of registration table.

Shred the Edge is back for its 9th year!

This is an unsanctioned race located at Camp Edge in Alloway, NJ. Proceeds from this race benefit Ranch Hope/Camp Edge and the Salem County Reactors Composite Mountain Bike Team.

Each loop is just over 4 miles in length with a mix of twists & turns, roots, and some hills. E-bikes are NOT permitted.

Advanced race - 4 laps (approx 16 miles) - this category is the equivalent to CAT 1/2 for both adults and youth.

Novice race - 2 laps (approx 8 miles) - this category is the equivalent to CAT 3/4 for both adults and youth.

Kids race - 1 lap (approx 3ish miles) - this category is for youth under the age of 12. This is the perfect category for racers who are too young to join NICA or who are new to the sport of mountain biking. The course will be modified to avoid technical areas and course marshals and sweepers will be present on the course to ensure everyone's safety.

Wake up lakeside by taking advantage of primitive camping for a small cash donation during race weekend. No electric or water hook-ups. Port-a-potties will be available.

Spectator friendly course!

We look forward to hosting everyone for Shred the Edge's NINTH year!

Element Adventures is proud to present Gritventure! 2, an adventure ride based out of our Element Adventures West Camp in Augusta, WV.  Featuring quiet gravel roads, stiff climbs, beautiful vistas, and backcountry riding, this ride will bring out the little kid in you!  This route will provide you with a tough challenge, but it will be well worth it!   Route details are below.

This will be a true gravel adventure: minimal SAG support, no route markings.  Download the GPX files so you can navigate the route (Cue sheets will also be provided).  There will be no aid stations set up, though there will be bars and gels available at the ride start to throw in your jersey pockets to take with you.  You'll need to carry enough water with you to last the ride or refill at stores or spigots found along the way.  You can refill bottles on the route at the Grassy Lick Kirby Community Center at a spigot.  Be prepared with flat changing tools and spare tubes, as gravel can be rough on tires (Some of the "roads" are now two grooves of singletrack!).  Take a cell phone, but be aware that service can be spotty.  This ride will go rain or shine, and being fall, there is always chance that it will be chilly and rainy.  Be prepared!

Suggested Equipment: A cyclocross or gravel / adventure bike with at least 32-40 mm tires would be your best choice.  A mountain bike would not even be out of place, especially on Short Mountain and Nathaniel Mountain for the Long and Medium routes.  You'll want a wide range of gearing, too, as some of the hills can be steep.  Helmets are required for all participants.

Cost: $25 through Oct 24, then $35 through Oct 30.  Day of registration will be $45.

Time: Check-in will be at 8:00 am through 10:00 am.  We will have a group start time of 8:30am if you would like to ride with the group.  You do not need to stay with the group. 

Food! Be sure to stay for the food and beer after the ride!

Directions to Element Adventures West Camp: From NoVA, take I-66 West to I-81 North to exit 310 (Route 37).  Take 37 North to Route 50 West.  Take Route 50 West through Augusta, WV.  Make a left onto McKee Hollow Road.  Take an almost immediate right onto South Fork of Little Cacapon Road.  In about 1.2 miles you will see a large mailbox with the address 1332.  Turn right up the driveway, and follow all the way up past the house and the barn to the parking area.  (Google Maps of South Fork of Little Cacapon road brings you just short of the address - you'll go a bit further to reach the driveway).  There will be an Element Adventures sign at the driveway.

 

Jerseys: Pre-order a jersey to commemorate this great ride!  These jerseys are full-zip and made of advanced moisture-wicking fabric to keep you cool and dry.  Rear pockets. Comfortable club fit available in mens and womens. You can order your jersey during registration.  $75. Size Charts below.

Greetings!

As 2025 comes to a close it’s time to gather and celebrate the year and start thinking about next. It’s time for our annual membership drive held at Reed’s Cycles (Boise location) on Bogus Basin Rd.

When: Thursday, December 4, 2025

Where: Reed’s Cycles, 2340 N Bogus Basin Rd, Boise

What time: 7-9 pm

Who is invited: all club member, non-members who are interested in finding out more about the club

What to expect:

  • learn more about the Lost River Cycling club

  • meet club members

  • talk about bikes

  • shop at Reed’s Cycles

  • sign-up to be a member

  • try on a Pactimo kit so that you can order the right size club kit (not obligatory)

  • great food and drinks (or at least pizza and beer)

We had a lot of successes in 2025, including: sponsoring our 3rd Annual Eagle Island Cyclocross race, a successful Over the Hill Gravel Grinder in Horseshoe Bend, the largest Cranksgiving Boise to date, the annual Jason Werst Century, organizing the Rhond van Boise, supporting the kid’s race at the Boise Twilight Criterium, organizing the Thorn Creek Gravel and Beer Ride, hosting weekly road and mountain bike rides, and hosted indoor rides all winter long.

For 2026 we plan on being back for all of these events, plus we’ve hoping to grow our weekly rides! We want more participation and more options for members. Part of 2026 will be reorganizing the club in the hopes of a larger involvement by a larger group of club members.

Come to the party on December 4th to learn more about the club, meet people, and talk about how you’d like to participate in club events. We’ll have pizza and drinks. It’s going to be a good time!

Sign up and ride with the Mohawk Hudson Cycling Club on Columbia County's magnificent gravel roads.  See the stunning autumn colors from the beautiful heights and rural valleys of this great gravel riding area. MHCC members and other cycling enthusiasts ride here all year and keep coming back for more.  PLUS, the first 130 who visit the registration desk will enjoy a sweet surprise treat from Bountiful Bread!!  Register soon, before the end of September, to avoid the $5 bump in the registration fee.

The four routes offer a full variety of ride types and challenges. Everyone can find the ride that's right!  A rest stop will be provided at the Red Rock Volunteer Fire Department for the 56 and 41 mile routes.  So you will have a place to rest and refuel before continuing your tour.  Note:  all participants are required to follow rules of the road for cycling and to wear a helmet.  As a safety tactic, each gravel ride will have a controlled, neutral start for the first mile.  Please review additional safety requirements and tips attached to your waiver. 

Also remember to download your chosen route to an on-board device or print out a cue sheet before you show up!

BONUS: There will be mechanical support onsite prior to the ride, courtesy of Karl Miller's  Blueline Spokes & Gears.

Make an additional donation online and/or come with a check, payable to Regional Food Bank of Northeastern NY.

Checkin begins at 8am at S&S Farm Brewery on November 1. 

After you finish, enjoy a craft beer at the S And S Farm Brewery and great food selections from the onsite food truck, available  from 12-3.  Remember to bring extra cash/card for your food and beverages.  

We expect you'll be famished at the end of your ride.  Park your bike and go directly to the SLIDIN' DIRTY Food Truck, parked near the Brewery, and order a meal and some finger food as a Goblin finish reward.

REMEMBER:  We will also be collecting checks (made out to the Regional Food Bank) and non-perishable food and personal care items on the day of the event.

About the Regional Food Bank:

The Regional Food Bank has been helping to feed the poor and hungry in our communities since 1982. It is the only organization of its kind in northeastern New York. The Food Bank collects large donations of food from the food industry and distributes it to charitable agencies serving hungry and disadvantaged people in 23 counties. From Plattsburgh to Newburgh, in urban, rural, and suburban communities, the Food Bank provides over 55 million pounds of food a year to 1,000 agencies. The Food Bank is a member of Feeding America, the national network of food banks. The Regional Food Bank is a non-profit organization, and all donations are tax-deductible to the fullest extent of the law.

Sunday November 1st 2026 is going to be a day to remember. We’re proud to bring you Cyclocross at Grand Island's premier Beaver Island State Park for yet another year. This place has all the goods including WNY’s best cyclocross sand pit, mixed riding surfaces, rolling terrain and beautiful waterfront views. Can you ride the beach? There’s only one way to find out! The history of Cyclocross at Beaver Island goes all the way back to Brenden Conway's Beaver Island Black Out! in 2012, No one who was there that day will ever forget that experience... 

Join us for a great day on the bike or spectating with friends and family. Beaver CX is not USAC Sanctioned so you do not need a race license to participate. Why would we do that? We wanted to reduce the barriers to entry. No race license means no extra fees for new racers. Less confusion and complications for our Canadian friends willing to cross the border. No reason not to come out of retirement if you happen to be an “experienced” racer that hasn't renewed their license for a couple years. All in all, a lot of reasons to race, very few reasons not to!

Racing will start at 10:30am with a course designed specifically for our Junior racers and continue through our final race of the day ending at or around 2pm. 

We will allow day of registration but ask you to please pre-register if possible. These events take many volunteers to run successfully and any and all preparation that can be done ahead of time makes these days run much smoother. Double up and race a second race for only $15!

The Stump Farm Mountain Bike Races are back for 2026 on November 1.   The 20 mile, three lap comp event starts at 10:00 and the one lap race starts at 10:10 for the FAT BIKE Category and 10:15 for the one lap 7 mile..  We have a mix of two track trail for passing and leaf blown single track on a full 7 mile plus loop. The Race direction in 2026 generally follows for the Normal trail flow; Counter Clockwise on the map with some added 2 track for passing early in the loop.

This is a small race with field limits so register early. Accordingly, there are no refunds for any reason.  Your registration is final. There are overall and age group awards.

Number plate pickup and concessions are inside the lodge.  We need the number plates back for the 2027 race.  Please help us with that!   

We ask you to self-seed in your start and be aware that the first transition to single track comes after a 0.8 mile roll out just like our August race, Refo Ramble.

We will leaf blow the course on Saturday, a bonus for all our area riders!  There are no aid stations.  We will have mobile course marshals and a medical cart.  

So, bring your own feeds for the race.  We will have Ahnapee Beer free if you show us a trail pass.  Garbage is carry in, carry out. 

Brown County is great at maintaining our trails with the help of the Friends of the Reforestation Camp Trails, one of your hosts!. To ride the trails, the County requires a daily or annual pass. For your convenience, if you don't have an annual pass already, you can pay us $5 below and show the ranger your receipt if you are asked. Otherwise you can buy a pass online or on site on race day or at the sign board just outside the lodge with a card or exact change. Trail fees support the trails.  We like that!  We will give you a beer/coffee ticket if you show us a trail pass as a thank you.  

Course marking will occur Friday to reinforce normal flow. There is no foot race this year.

The event host is the Green Bay Trailblazers, with Friends of the Reforestation Camp Trails,  and Ashwaubenon Nordic Ski Team partnering again.  Your race volunteers are the from FoRCT, Trailblazers and ANST.

WE'RE BACK FOR OUR 14TH YEAR! and excited to announce that the Fourteethn edition of WCCX will be held on Sunday November 1st at famous Ludwig’s Corner Horse Show and Fairgrounds.  This location has special history...utilized by Wissahickon Cross (including UCI races) for several years last held in 2009, and more recently the home of WCCX since 2018.  For 2026, WCCX is celebrating it's 14th anniversary!

Cyclocross is a fun and physically demanding type of bicycle racing. EventNotes:
The Dirty Pilgrim

A Gravel Ride for the People!

Although over shadowed by less significant events at the time, upon their arrival in Plymouth the Pilgrims found more than a mere "rock" upon which they hoped to land all their dreams. Rather, they found a rich & diverse countryside laced with miles of idyllic gravel roads, accented by scenic vistas, and punctuated with an abundance of fine craft brews & richly roasted coffee. Building upon that spirit of adventure & excitement that they felt that day, we now present for your entertainment and pedaling enjoyment, The Dirty Pilgrim. 

Ladies & gentlemen, early-risers & thrill seekers, snack enthusiasts & coffee fiends... Let us all now go in peace and Pedal in Dirt.  May the Grit Be With You.  

-Amen

About:
The Dirty Pilgrim is the brainchild of longtime South Shore gravel aficionados Steve Cobble, Brian Carlson, & Dave Farrell. They're constantly looking to explore old trails, find new routes to ride, and always doing so with with less pavement involved.  Now although some group led rides will be available, in general you should be comfortable with self-navigating via GPS or plan on riding with someone who is.  To that end, be sure to bring ample food & water, spare tubes & inflators, a fully charged cell phone, and a healthy “can do” attitude.  We'll see you out there!

Dear gravel riders, soul surfers & anyone who uses the bike to  escape time... 

It's Heidi Rentz & Zander Ault here...

We are co-creators of The Spirit World 100 & The Cyclist's Menu, gravel cyclists, chefs & party animals. We're so freaking excited to see you in Patagonia, Arizona for a gravel road race that has inspired every aspect of our lives.

The Arizona Borderlands are known for it's rugged, stunning landscapes & views that you'd never guess existed. You have to see it with your own eyes! Throughout the Spirit World 30, 50, 80, & 100 mile courses - you'll climb up + down & around elevations that range between 4,000 - 6,000 feet above sea level. The San Rafael Valleys demanding terrain asks that you keep your head up at all times. It will be bumpy, winds will always be changing their minds, descents will leave you speechless, and climbs will guide you farther into the Spirit World.

Don't hesitate to reach out with thoughts/questions/ideas... any time. We can't wait to ride bikes and eat food with you this November!

Why does it cost $255 for the 30, 50, 80, & 100 mile race? ??

This special event is capped at only 250 riders & we intend to keep it this small. It's our biggest goal to make it feel like an intimate gathering for 4 days of goodness.

We care deeply about inviting you to experience something you haven't experienced before. 

You won't be disappointed :)
